To doubt the distinction is to doubt from a standpoint that distinguishes the doubting from what is doubted, to instantiate the distinction in the denying. The embodied demonstration that follows runs the same structural point at the bodily level, for any reader whose standpoint includes bilateral haptic differentiation; readers without that particular embodiment have the universal anchor above as the load-bearing phenomenological access.

Consider the act of reading this sentence. Your left hand rests here; your right hand rests here. Two heres, simultaneous, both yours, both demonstratively accessible from a single standpoint. Look at one of them and feel it at once; now feel it more than you see it, then see it more than you feel it. The hand has not moved. The standpoint has. The plurality is not inferred; it is given in the very having of the standpoint (plural positions, plural channels, plural weightings) and there is no possible performance of doubt from which the articulation could be coherently dismissed, because the doubt itself distinguishes the thought (here) from its object (there), the attending mind from the attended content. To doubt from a standpoint is to doubt from a standpoint with internal articulation. Unarticulated standpoints have nothing from which to doubt.

Plural heres cannot be distinct without something grounding their distinctness. By the identity of indiscernibles, two heres with nothing distinguishing them are one here, not two. The only available ground of distinctness at the positional level is relational: positions individuated by how they stand to one another, not by intrinsic content that differs. The plurality of heres therefore just is the instantiation of relational extension, delivered from the inside, first-person, undeniable in the performance.

*The impossibility argument.* Any act that produces spatial extension thereby instantiates the full spatial logic (the foreclosure of square circles, the exclusivity of positional occupancy) constitutive of what extension is, not an addition after the fact. An originating act that produces Spatiality is not prior to or independent of Spatiality but an exercise of it; there can be no particular place without Spatiality already in place. The point can be stated formally:

::: {.argument}
**Spatiality** · *The N_S Reductio.* Let Px abbreviate *x is placed*; let S abbreviate *Spatiality is instantiated*; let N_S abbreviate *there was never no Spatiality*.

1. Any placing requires Spatiality, since *placed* presupposes a relational interval between positions (∀x(Px → S)).

1. Something is placed: there is at least one placing, demonstrably the plural *heres* of the present standpoint (∃xPx).

1. So Spatiality is instantiated (∴ S; from 1, 2).

1. If there were ever no Spatiality, then Spatiality would have to be placed or introduced, since a transition from no-S to S is itself a placing (¬N_S → P(S)).

1. Any placing or introduction of Spatiality would already require Spatiality, applying line 1 to S itself (P(S) → S).

1. So there was never no Spatiality: ¬N_S entails P(S), and P(S) entails S-prior-to-S, a contradiction (∴ N_S; from 4, 5 by reductio).

:::

In plain terms: locations can be assigned within Spatiality, but Spatiality cannot be assigned a location from no-Spatiality. The transition from no-where to where already uses the relation it claims to introduce.

The actuality-to-necessity bridge runs through lines 4–6 specifically: line 2 supplies actuality (∃xPx), but the necessity result N_S does not follow from actuality alone. It follows from the conceptual closure that any candidate alternative (¬N_S) generates a contradiction: the alternative would require Spatiality-prior-to-Spatiality to instantiate itself, which the Parasitic Negation rules out. N_S is therefore necessary by conceptual closure of the alternative, not by extrapolation from ∃xPx.

This is **Parasitic Negation** ([§2.1.5](the-argument.html#sec-2-1-5)) instantiated to S: relational extension cannot emerge from no-extension, since any placing would already instantiate the relations it claims to introduce. This reductio is one of two roads to the necessity of Spatiality; the modal line reaches the same conclusion jointly at [§2.5](the-argument.html#sec-2-5), where □(T∧S∧Φ) unpacks into the Necessity of Spatiality (□S).

*What is established.* Succession and extension are derived. Neither survives without something carrying the influence from one to the other.[^2-4-7-spatiality-ch4]

[^2-4-7-spatiality-ch4]: The objections to the spatial Condition are engaged in Chapter 4: bundle theory and tropes, which deny relational positions as fundamental ([§4.3.10](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-10)), mereological nihilism, which denies extended composites ([§4.3.11](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-11)), haecceitism and primitive thisness, which ground distinctness without relational extension ([§4.3.12](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-12)), Sider's structuralism on relational extension ([§4.4.7](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-4-7)), and Platonist aspatiality ([§4.2.4](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-2-4)).

### 2.4.8 Exchange Requires Physicality {#sec-2-4-8}

Succession and distinction were derived at §[§2.4.6](the-argument.html#sec-2-4-6)–2.4.7. The third Condition (a medium of causal persistence) follows from what those two already require: for influence to be transmitted across genuinely distinct states, something must carry it. That carrier is Physicality, defined at [§1.4.3](groundwork.html#sec-1-4-3) and borne in Reality by Substance.

The argument states this load-bearing commitment openly, as an explicit premise rather than an implicit assumption:

**Constitutive Premise (Cross-Interval Persistence).** Genuine exchange just *is* carriage across an interval: for influence to pass from one state to the next is for something to persist across the interval and bear it, not merely for two states to be correlated. Any account that grants the exchange while blocking the physical conclusion must deny precisely this identification, and that denial is costly, as the argument below shows.

*The exclusivity argument.* Suppose exclusive occupancy is a primitive geometric fact: two configurations cannot occupy the same coordinate, and nothing enforces it. What makes the incompatibility real rather than merely described? If nothing prevents double occupancy, the exclusivity is nominal, not structural. If the presence of one configuration forecloses another, the foreclosure is causal in the broad sense: something is doing the excluding, and that cross-interval operation is what Φ names. Either exclusive occupancy is real and underwritten by some cross-interval operation, or it is nominal and not exclusive at all.

A primitivist about exclusion might press a third option: exclusivity is real and primitive, neither causal in the canonical event-to-event sense nor nominal. The reply runs the same way as the response to primitivism about laws [below, with @maudlin2007]. Whatever makes a primitive exclusion *do* exclusion-work must operate across the foreclosure interval: distinguishing the present configuration from the foreclosed alternative, holding the foreclosure stable across the interval where the foreclosed configuration is foreclosed. That cross-interval operation is what Φ names at the level of foreclosure rather than at the level of explicit event causation. The primitivist who keeps the foreclosure stable inherits the medium-work under different vocabulary; the primitivist who strips the cross-interval operation loses what makes the exclusion an exclusion rather than a label. The bridge from exclusivity to Φ is therefore not the claim that exclusion is *the same as* canonical event causation. It is the claim that exclusion, to do exclusion-work, requires the cross-interval persistence that Φ names, whether that work is read as causal in the standard sense or as a primitive foreclosure that performs the same structural function.

Causal exchange further requires distinct causal terms or roles. The source-state and uptake-state cannot collapse into one undifferentiated term, but they need not belong to two numerically distinct beings: one persisting system may occupy both roles at different stages. Physicality requires a real distinction between initiation and reception, not an exclusion of self-interaction or internal change.

*The momentariness reply.* The objection that reality consists of momentary non-persisting events with lawlike relations between them does not eliminate Physicality; it relocates it. A lawlike relation requires the medium to be configured such that events of type A reliably produce events of type B. That configurational reliability just *is* Physicality at the level of the medium rather than the object. Dissolve Physicality at the object level and it reappears at the medium level: what bears the modal force the regularity requires. Hume's denial of necessary connection between distinct existences does not dispense with the medium; it declines to name what his regularities presuppose.

Primitivism about laws [@maudlin2007; @beebeeHitchcockMenzies2009] reaches the same result from the other direction. Whatever makes a primitive law govern must itself persist across the causal interval, differentiate its relata, and host the direction from ground to grounded; that is Physicality, given stronger ontological standing than the Humean was willing to extend.

*The vocabulary case.* Ordinary causal vocabulary carries the structural Triconditions in its morphology. Static nouns name the medium: *resistance* and *yielding* (holding under transition or giving way), *consistency* (succession running without lapse), *coherence* (states held in exchange). Verbs name the acts inside change: *cause*, *effect*, *push*, *pull*, *mix*. Each word denotes only the kind of change defined at [§1.3](groundwork.html#sec-1-3); subtract the medium and the words stop carrying meaning.

*Push* and *pull* carry the commitment most concretely. *Push*: to exert force away from the agent. *Pull*: to exert force toward the agent. Each names three relations in a single one-syllable verb: an agent, a patient, and an interval across which force transfers between them. Remove any one and neither verb denotes. No agent: a force without source. No patient: a force with nowhere to go. No interval: two things at the same coordinate, which is not a relation at all. Both verbs commit the speaker to T (the force takes a moment), S (agent and patient stand apart), and Φ (something carries the force across) before the sentence finishes. *Resistance* and *yielding* run the same three commitments from the receiving side: what holds against the force or gives way under it. *Cause* runs them abstractly: a producing-relation requires something to produce, something produced, and an interval across which the producing reaches. The vocabulary is not neutral evidence of the structure but its signature in the language used to describe and dispute it.

*The deflationary case.* It proposes that *cause* names nothing beyond constant conjunction: events of type A regularly followed by events of type B, with no producing-relation underwriting the pattern [@hume1748, §VII; @lewis1986; @loewer1996; @beebee2006]. The proposal deserves its strongest reading: declining to posit invisible connective tissue is not carelessness but discipline. Three layers of reply are available.

*Statement.* The reduction cannot be stated without what it tries to subtract. *Event B regularly follows event A* requires Temporality (B after A), Spatiality (an interval between them), and Physicality (an observer persisting long enough to note the regularity). The reduction subtracts the structure in its conclusion and spends it in its premise. The deflationary vocabulary is parasitic on the structure it means to replace.

*Morphology.* The ordinary word *impression* has a historical association with pressing, but etymology does not determine the term's technical content in empiricist theory. That association may serve as a mnemonic for the experiential contact the word often evokes; it cannot establish that an empiricist is analytically committed to a pressing-relation. The morphology layer is therefore only a non-probative illustration and carries no argumentative weight. The Statement and Inference layers carry the structural point independently.

*Inference.* At a third level, the argument runs on what it denies. Arguments require persistence (premises must hold across the inferential interval) and exchange (premises must yield conclusions in one direction). Persistence and exchange are what Physicality contributes. To argue against the producing-relation is to deploy producing in the deriving.

The three replies (statement, morphology, inference) establish that the deflationary vocabulary cannot be stated, motivated, or argued for without instantiating T, S, and Φ wherever the case is made. The narrower claim is actuality at the site of statement; the move to necessity across worlds where no case is made is taken up at §§3–6 (Humean modal-contingency at [§4.1.4](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-4)).

The foregoing arguments carry the load; the phenomenological anchor that follows is offered, like the demonstrations at §[§2.4.6](the-argument.html#sec-2-4-6)–2.4.7, as confirmation rather than proof. The most universal anchor for Physicality runs at the level of the thinker holding the thought, prior to any embodied bearing. Any conscious standpoint has the relation directly: a thought does not float free; it is held in being by whatever is having it. The thinker is not the thought; the thinker is what bears the thought across the interval of its occurring. Strip out the bearer and what remains is a sentence-shaped description of a thought, not a thought; a thought-without-a-bearer is not a thought that happens to lack one, it is the absence of a thought, with only the form of one in language. The relation is undeniable in the strong Cartesian sense: to deny that the thinker holds the thought is to perform a thought that is, in the performing, held; the denier is the holder doing the work the denial would have to escape.

*The impossibility argument.* Any act that produces Physicality must already instantiate it: there is no prior position from which to generate causal persistence without occupying it. The point can be stated formally:

::: {.argument}
**Physicality** · *The N_Φ Reductio.* Let Px abbreviate *x is produced*; let Φ abbreviate *Physicality is instantiated*; let N_Φ abbreviate *there was never no Physicality*.

1. Any production requires Physicality, since *produced* presupposes a medium carrying influence across an interval (∀x(Px → Φ)).

1. Something has been produced: there is at least one production, demonstrably the thinker holding the present thought (∃xPx).

1. So Physicality is instantiated (∴ Φ; from 1, 2).

1. If there were ever no Physicality, then Physicality would have to be produced, since a transition from no-Φ to Φ is itself a production (¬N_Φ → P(Φ)).

1. Any production of Physicality would already require Physicality, applying line 1 to Φ itself (P(Φ) → Φ).

1. So there was never no Physicality: ¬N_Φ entails P(Φ), and P(Φ) entails Φ-prior-to-Φ, a contradiction (∴ N_Φ; from 4, 5 by reductio).

:::

In plain terms: products can arise within Physicality, but Physicality cannot be produced from no-Physicality. Production is already the causal persistence Physicality names.

The actuality-to-necessity bridge runs through lines 4–6 specifically: line 2 supplies actuality (∃xPx), but the necessity result N_Φ does not follow from actuality alone. It follows from the conceptual closure that any candidate alternative (¬N_Φ) generates a contradiction: the alternative would require Physicality-prior-to-Physicality to instantiate itself, which the Parasitic Negation rules out. N_Φ is therefore necessary by conceptual closure of the alternative, not by extrapolation from ∃xPx.

This is **Parasitic Negation** ([§2.1.5](the-argument.html#sec-2-1-5)) instantiated to Φ: causal persistence cannot emerge from its own absence, since any act of producing it would already instantiate it. The same move runs at chapter scope at [§3.4](convergence.html#sec-3-4); it is deployed for the Φ-incoherence of ∅ at [§2.7.1](the-argument.html#sec-2-7-1). This reductio is one of two roads to the necessity of Physicality; the modal line reaches the same conclusion jointly at [§2.5](the-argument.html#sec-2-5), where □(T∧S∧Φ) unpacks into the Necessity of Physicality (□Φ).

*What is established.* With Physicality in place, the three Conditions are derived. Succession, distinction, and the medium that carries them arrived together: each required by the same structural fact, not three independent claims. That they arrived is established. Whether they could have failed to arrive is the remaining question.[^2-4-8-physicality-ch4]

[^2-4-8-physicality-ch4]: The objections to the physical Condition are engaged in Chapter 4: Russellian monism ([§4.3.3](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-3)), idealism ([§4.3.5](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-5)), bundle theory and tropes ([§4.3.10](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-10)), and mereological nihilism ([§4.3.11](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-11)). The hard problem, as an alleged consciousness-substrate outside structural exhaustion, is taken up at [§4.3.1](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-1).

### 2.4.9 Forward Conditional Necessity {#sec-2-4-9}

The forward conditional is stated as a necessary conditional: **□(◇C → (T∧S∧Φ))**. Not merely true in every possible world: structurally necessary. No possible world could satisfy the antecedent without the consequent. Three aspects establish this, and they converge on the same structural fact.

The *structural aspect:* modal facts are structural facts about Reality. The definitions (T as causally structured succession, S as relational extension, Φ as causal persistence) are not descriptions of contingent physical processes. They are what it structurally means to host change. A world in which change is possible but succession is absent is not a world with unusual physics. It is a world in which change is incoherent, which means it is not a world in which change is possible. The Δ argument of [§2.4.5](the-argument.html#sec-2-4-5) grounds this as framework-invariant: any theory that describes a Reality where change is possible is bound by the same structural constraints.

The *conceptual aspect:* to deny the conditional is to assert that a concept applies in the absence of its own defining conditions. Change without succession. Movement without extension. Interaction without persistence. This is not an unusual possible world. It is a contradiction in terms, in the same sense that a square circle is: not because every world happens to exclude it, but because its denial is not a coherent description of any world.

The *essential aspect:* the definitions are constitutive of essences, not merely reference-fixing descriptions. There is no deeper essence of change hiding behind the definitions. The concept and the essence coincide, not at the level of language but at the level of structural Conditions. A world where change lacks its essential structural requirements is a world where change is something other than change.

@fine1994 argues that essence is prior to modality rather than derivable from it: the essence of a thing is what that thing is by virtue of its own nature, and necessities about the thing follow from its essence rather than grounding it. The essential aspect above endorses Fine's priority claim for the case of T, S, and Φ. The definitions in §[§1.3](groundwork.html#sec-1-3)–1.4 are not modal stipulations from which the essences of change, Temporality, Spatiality, and Physicality follow as a consequence; they are direct specifications of what those phenomena are. The necessity □(◇C → (T∧S∧Φ)) is derivative: it holds because of what change, T, S, and Φ essentially are, not because a modal axiom has been stipulated to make it hold. This is why denying the conditional does not describe an unusual world: it describes no world, because the antecedent's own content already requires the consequent.

*What converges.* The three aspects are not independent paths to the same destination. They are the same structural fact viewed from every direction at which necessity has content. The forward conditional is not a fact about this universe. It is a fact about what any universe must be. And the fact is level-invariant in the sense established at [§2.4.3](the-argument.html#sec-2-4-3): whether a given Reality is described physically, as content, or as mental activity, the conditional runs through all three descriptions without remainder, because what it requires (succession, distinction, exchange) is not a feature of any description but of what any description is a description of.[^2-4-9-forward-conditional-necessity-ch4]

[^2-4-9-forward-conditional-necessity-ch4]: The necessity claim is challenged on several fronts in Chapter 4: the Principle of Sufficient Reason offers a rival ground of necessity ([§4.1.3](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-3)); Quine denies the analytic–essential distinction the essential aspect relies on ([§4.1.6](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-6)); conventionalism treats necessity as stipulated rather than structural ([§4.1.7](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-7)); the source-of-possibility question asks whether possibility has an independent source ([§4.1.10](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-10)); and Williamson's necessitism stands as the over-strong rival ([§4.4.6](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-4-6)).

### 2.4.10 Sufficiency of Structure {#sec-2-4-10}

The forward conditional (§[§2.4.5](the-argument.html#sec-2-4-5)–2.4.9) established the left-to-right direction: if change is possible, T∧S∧Φ are instantiated. The converse also holds: **(T∧S∧Φ) → ◇C**. If T∧S∧Φ are instantiated, change is possible. The two together form the biconditional reading: **◇C ↔ (T∧S∧Φ)**, not two facts that happen to coincide, but one fact described from two sides.

Temporality is instantiated if and only if causally structured succession among states obtains. But causally structured succession among states is exactly what change requires: one state following another through directed causal influence. To say Temporality is instantiated is to say the succession-condition for change is met. The same applies to Spatiality (traversable relational extension = the distinction-condition) and Physicality (causal persistence = the exchange-condition). The Conditions do not accompany change's possibility. They spell it out.

The contrast here is with a weaker claim: that structure permits change. *Permits* treats T, S, and Φ as a neutral scaffold compatible with either change or no-change, leaving open a fully-instantiated-but-static structure. *Enables*, as meant here, is stronger: the instantiation of T, S, and Φ just is the availability of transitions. Change is not a further fact to be added, nor a dormant possibility the structure passively accommodates. It is what the instantiation of the Conditions amounts to. The circularity worry (that this makes the result definitional) is taken up below.

The ground for this identity is the account established in [§2.4.1](the-argument.html#sec-2-4-1). Modal facts are structural facts about Reality within which possible worlds are defined. The possibility of change is a structural fact: whether Reality permits causally structured succession. The instantiation of Temporality is a structural fact: whether causally structured succession obtains in Reality. These are not two independently obtained facts that happen to coincide; they are two descriptions of the same structural ground.

The point is not merely that instantiation is compatible with change-possibility but that the causal character of the Conditions is constitutive rather than dormant: their instantiation is their activity. A structure with genuine causal directedness is one in which directed influence is its own structural character, not a further possibility layered onto inert geometry.

The strongest challenge to the converse asks whether structure could be fully present yet change still foreclosed. Four objections raise this question: at the level of frozen worlds, dispositional masking, definitional guarantees, and the attempt to specify a foreclosing constraint without contradiction. Each fails in a different way.

*The frozen-world objection* ([§2.4.11](the-argument.html#sec-2-4-11)) and *the masking objection* ([§2.4.12](the-argument.html#sec-2-4-12)) press the strongest forms of this concern at the level of dedicated subsections. Both fail in the same way: the Conditions as defined require causal structure, and a *world* stripped of that structure does not instantiate T, S, and Φ in a paralyzed mode; it fails to instantiate them at all.

*The trivialization concern.* If the Conditions are defined causally, of course their instantiation entails causal possibility. But the causal dimensions were not inserted to guarantee the result. They were established in [§1.4](groundwork.html#sec-1-4) because without them the Conditions fail to do what they are supposed to do.

A *Temporality* without causal directionality does not host succession. A *Spatiality* without traversability does not host distinction. A *Physicality* without causal persistence does not host exchange. The definitions track what the Conditions structurally require. That their instantiation generates change-possibility is a consequence of what they are, not of how they were defined.

*Can a foreclosing constraint be specified without contradiction?* The circularity charge can be made precise, and precisely answered. Suppose T, S, and Φ are genuinely instantiated (causally structured succession obtains, relational extension obtains, causal persistence obtains) but ◇C is false: no change is possible. What structural feature of such a world forecloses change?

The options are exhaustive. Either the foreclosure removes a causal dimension from one of the Conditions (directedness from succession, traversability from extension, causal connection from persistence) in which case the Condition is no longer instantiated as defined and the antecedent is false.

Or the foreclosure adds an external constraint that blocks change despite full instantiation of the Conditions. But any such constraint, fully unpacked, forecloses causally structured succession among states of a persisting subject across a relational interval, which is the negation of T∧S∧Φ under a different description. A constraint that leaves T, S, and Φ intact while blocking what their instantiation structurally generates asserts and denies the same structural fact. It is like asking for a triangle that both has and lacks three sides under the same specification: not a difficult triangle but a contradictory one. No coherent specification of the foreclosing constraint survives: every candidate either removes a causal dimension (falsifying the antecedent) or restates the negation of T∧S∧Φ (contradicting the supposition). The supposition is not merely false. It is incoherent.

*Modality at the primitive level.* The strongest version of the circularity charge presses one level deeper: that to say *causality is what causal relata are* smuggles modality in at a deeper level. Every framework needs primitives. This one's primitive is that causal structure is irreducibly causal, not a modal overlay on something non-causal underneath. And this primitive is uniquely self-supporting: denying it is itself a causal act, performed through the causal structure being denied. Any attempt to contest the claim already relies on the relation it contests.

The critic who calls the proof circular must transition from not-seeing-circularity to claiming it (T), distinguish the premise from the accusation (S), and persist as the same thinker throughout (Φ). The charge is delivered on the structure it contests.

*Result.* ◇C and T∧S∧Φ are two descriptions of the same structural ground. There is no gap between them. The biconditional **◇C ↔ (T∧S∧Φ)** is established.

Three pieces are now in hand and should be kept distinct on the path to the chapter-level conclusion. The Cartesian certainty of change's possibility ([§2.2](the-argument.html#sec-2-2)) grants ◇C as a proposition. The forward conditional ◇C → (T∧S∧Φ), established at §[§2.4.5](the-argument.html#sec-2-4-5)–2.4.9, is the left-to-right direction of the biconditional; modus ponens on that certainty and the forward conditional yields T∧S∧Φ. The converse T∧S∧Φ → ◇C (the right-to-left direction) closes the biconditional reading ◇C ↔ (T∧S∧Φ). Combined with the necessity of the conditional ([§2.4.9](the-argument.html#sec-2-4-9)) and the Necessary Possibility of Change □◇C ([§2.3](the-argument.html#sec-2-3)), the unconditional □(T∧S∧Φ) follows at the chapter level. What remains (the unconditional necessity of Nature) is the final declaration at [§2.8.5](the-argument.html#sec-2-8-5), which combines the biconditional, the chapter's modal-invariance results ([§2.3](the-argument.html#sec-2-3), supplemented by the ∅ Reductio at [§2.7.4](the-argument.html#sec-2-7-4)), and the structural identity of T∧S∧Φ with Nature ([§2.6.10](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-10)). Establishing the converse direction closes the biconditional; the unconditional theorem itself follows only at [§2.8.5](the-argument.html#sec-2-8-5).[^2-4-10-sufficiency-of-structure-ch4]

[^2-4-10-sufficiency-of-structure-ch4]: The converse (that structure suffices for change-possibility) is engaged in Chapter 4: Sider's structuralism ([§4.4.7](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-4-7)), structural realism ([§4.3.9](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-9)), Tegmark's mathematical universe ([§4.3.7](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-7)), the changeless ground ([§4.2.1](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-2-1)), and the block universe ([§4.2.6](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-2-6)).

### 2.4.11 The Frozen-World Test {#sec-2-4-11}

Suppose a world has the right-looking structure but is permanently frozen: nothing ever changes, nothing can change. It looks like a world that instantiates T, S, and Φ with change ruled out: a standing counterexample to the converse ([§2.4.10](the-argument.html#sec-2-4-10)). The appearance dissolves the moment the Conditions are read as defined.

They require causal structure (directed succession, traversable extension, causal persistence), and a frozen world has static ordering, geometry, and fixed configuration, but none of the causal dimensions that make the Conditions what they are.

The same diagnosis applies individually to each Condition. Temporality without directedness is not paralyzed Temporality but static ordering, and static ordering is not Temporality, because Temporality ([§1.4](groundwork.html#sec-1-4)) is causally structured succession with direction and weight; a structure stripped of direction has lost what makes succession a succession rather than a fixed sequence-relation among items. Spatiality without traversability is not paralyzed Spatiality but static geometry, and static geometry is not Spatiality, because Spatiality ([§1.4](groundwork.html#sec-1-4)) is relational extension across which traversal is possible; a geometry stripped of traversability is a set of points standing in fixed distance-relations, not relational extension in the constitutive sense. Physicality without causal connection is not paralyzed Physicality but fixed configuration, and fixed configuration is not Physicality, because Physicality ([§1.4](groundwork.html#sec-1-4)) is causal persistence (a substance carrying causal power across T-succession through S-extension); a configuration stripped of causal capacity has lost what makes substance carry causal power rather than occupy a labeled position in a fixed array. Strip causality out and you do not get a frozen version of T, S, and Φ. You get something else entirely: three new structural specifications that share the names but not the constitutive content of the Conditions.

*What is foreclosed.* The consequence for the converse ([§2.4.10](the-argument.html#sec-2-4-10)) is direct: a world that genuinely instantiates the Conditions cannot fail to permit change, because the Conditions just are what permitting change consists in. The frozen-world scenario describes the absence of the Conditions, not their unusual mode.[^2-4-11-frozen-world-ch4]

[^2-4-11-frozen-world-ch4]: Shoemaker’s canonical staggered-freeze argument for time without change is engaged at [§4.2.2](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-2-2).

### 2.4.12 The Masking Test {#sec-2-4-12}

T, S, and Φ are the structure within which dispositions and masks operate, not localized dispositions that can themselves be masked.

A dispositionalist [@bird2007; @mumfordAnjum2011] might reply that the causal dimensions could be genuine but permanently unmanifested: fragility in a glass never struck. On the dispositionalist picture, masks and antidotes are familiar features of the world: a fragile glass wrapped in foam does not break when dropped, but its fragility is not thereby absent. So perhaps the structural Conditions could be present in the world while their characteristic outputs (succession, distinction, exchange) are universally masked.

The disanalogy is structural. T, S, and Φ are not localized dispositions within Nature; they are the structural context within which every disposition, masking condition, and interference operates. The stronger reading that T∧S∧Φ *is* Nature in the full Triconditional sense is established at [§2.6.10](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-10) with the Triconditional Identity theorem; the dialectical foreclosure here requires only the weaker structural-context-vs-localized-disposition distinction. A localized disposition (fragility, solubility, irritability) is a property attaching to a Φ-bearer at an S-position over T-succession; the structural context is what makes property-attaching possible at all. The masking machinery operates on properties within the structural context; it has no application to the structural context itself. A masking condition for the Conditions would require a structural outside to structure. There is no such outside. The fragility of the glass is masked by the foam because the foam, the glass, and the dropping all share the structure that lets a mask be a mask. Strip the structure and there is nothing for the mask to operate within.

The same diagnosis applies to global-constraint variants: a necessary law that permits T, S, and Φ but forbids all transitions asserts the causal character of Nature while denying what that character structurally amounts to. A constraint that leaves the Conditions intact while blocking what they generate asserts and denies the same structural fact. The specification is incoherent, not difficult.

*What is foreclosed.* The masking move is not rejected because it is theoretically misguided; the dispositionalist literature it draws from [@martin1994; @bird2007; @mumfordAnjum2011] is sound at the level it operates. It fails at the structural level because the move requires a structural outside that the very category of structure forecloses.[^2-4-12-structural-masking-ch4]

[^2-4-12-structural-masking-ch4]: The masking-foreclosure result (that T, S, and Φ are the structural context within which every disposition and mask operates, not localized dispositions that can themselves be masked) is engaged in Chapter 4. Schaffer's priority monism is taken up through the constitutive-versus-productive grounding distinction in the Modal Collapse Objection ([§4.4.9](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-4-9)), and ontic structural realism engages structure-as-primitive from the relational side ([§4.3.9](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-9)).

## 2.5 Triconditional Necessity {#sec-2-5}

Two results already earned now meet: change is possible in every possible world ([§2.3](the-argument.html#sec-2-3)), and any world with possible change must have the three Conditions ([§2.4](the-argument.html#sec-2-4)). Together they entail that the three Conditions themselves hold in every possible world. They cannot fail to be there. This is the step that makes the joint structure necessary. The stronger identification of that structure as one Nature is established in [§2.6](the-argument.html#sec-2-6), and its identity with Reality is assembled at [§2.8](the-argument.html#sec-2-8).

The result is delivered by a single line that runs the length of the chapter so far. The Cartesian certainty that change is possible (◇C, [§2.2](the-argument.html#sec-2-2)) is lifted by the Necessary Possibility Theorem ([§2.1.10](the-argument.html#sec-2-1-10)) into its necessitated form, the Necessary Possibility of Change □◇C ([§2.3](the-argument.html#sec-2-3)). The possibility of change holds at every world in the fixed global domain W. The Structural Requirement, □(◇C → (T∧S∧Φ)) ([§2.4](the-argument.html#sec-2-4)), states that necessarily the possibility of change cannot obtain except where the three Conditions are instantiated at the resolution the individual Condition arguments establish.

The two close by a single modal step: the Structural Requirement is a *necessitated conditional* and the Necessary Possibility of Change its *necessitated antecedent*, so necessity distributes over the conditional. That distribution is the K axiom, valid in every normal modal logic and so *a fortiori* in the S5 the proof runs in: □(◇C → (T∧S∧Φ)) → (□◇C → □(T∧S∧Φ)). Assembled end to end, the line runs:

::: {.argument}
**Triconditional Necessity** · *The Full Line*

1. *Necessary Possibility (T1).* Real possibility ranges over one fixed domain W, so whatever is possible is necessarily possible. ◇P → □◇P

1. *Cartesian Certainty.* Change is possible, certain at the very level of its own denial. ◇C

1. From (1): apply the theorem to change itself. ◇C → □◇C

1. *Necessary Possibility of Change (L3).* From (2) and (3), modus ponens necessitates the possibility of change. □◇C

1. *Structural Requirement.* Necessarily, the possibility of change cannot obtain without the three Conditions. □(◇C → (T∧S∧Φ))

1. From (5): the K axiom carries necessity across the conditional. □◇C → □(T∧S∧Φ)

1. **Triconditional Necessity.** From (4) and (6), modus ponens delivers the result: the three Conditions hold of necessity. □(T∧S∧Φ)

:::

Step 7 is the result: the three Conditions are not a feature the actual world happens to carry but hold at every member of the fixed global domain of real possibility. The conclusion concerns the role- and type-level Conditions established in [§2.4](the-argument.html#sec-2-4), not particular metrics, geometries, fields, or occupants. Stated as the standing result the rest of the chapter draws on:

::: {.corollary}
**Triconditional Necessity** · **R5** · *Result of L3, SR*

Temporality, Spatiality, and Physicality are co-instantiated in every possible world, because the possibility of change (itself necessary) cannot obtain without them. This stage establishes the necessity of their joint presence: □(T∧S∧Φ). Section 2.6 argues that the joint structure is one Nature; [§2.8](the-argument.html#sec-2-8) then assembles the identity of Nature and Reality.


:::

*Where this sits, and why it is also a premise.* The result is a stage, not the terminus. The argument moves in three stages. *Stage 1* established that the possibility of change is necessary: □◇C ([§2.3](the-argument.html#sec-2-3)). *Stage 2*, reached here, establishes that the conditions on which that possibility depends are themselves necessary: □(T∧S∧Φ), the Triconditional Necessity. *Stage 3* is the capstone, the stronger claim the whole argument is built toward: that **Reality and Nature are one and the same**, that Nature is not a necessary endowment Reality happens to carry, but what Reality consists in, with nothing real lying outside it.

Between Stage 2 and that capstone, the next section ([§2.6](the-argument.html#sec-2-6)) takes up what this result identifies (that Temporality, Spatiality, and Physicality are not three separate facts but one Nature read three ways), establishing the Triconditional Identity ([§2.6.10](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-10)) and earning the full biconditional whose forward leg alone carries this stage.

This is just why the result is a premise as well as a conclusion: □(T∧S∧Φ) closes Line 1, and it is the premise Stage 3 takes up, at [§2.8](the-argument.html#sec-2-8), where the necessity established here is shown to exhaust the real and to leave the Null State ([§2.7](the-argument.html#sec-2-7)) as no genuine alternative.

*Scope.* Two limits travel with the premise. The necessity is de dicto with respect to the structural constraint (necessarily, any possible Reality instantiates T, S, and Φ), not a de re necessity of this universe, its constants, or any configuration it hosts. And it attaches to the structural roles, not to their occupants: contingency within necessity is preserved ([§2.8.4](the-argument.html#sec-2-8-4)). Nature is necessary; what fills it is not.

::: {.column-margin .book-annotation-note}
**Natural worry.** Doesn't this prove far too much—that the universe, with just these constants and contents, couldn't have been otherwise? No, and two limits travel with the result. First, the necessity is de dicto: what's necessary is that any possible reality instantiates time, space, and persistence—not that this universe, its particular constants, or any configuration it hosts had to be. Second, it attaches to the structural roles, not to their occupants. The roles hold in every world; what fills them varies freely. So contingency is preserved right where you'd want it: Nature is necessary, but what fills Nature is not. The claim is about the frame, not the furniture.

:::


*The three, taken singly.* The result is stated jointly because that is how the chain delivers it, but necessity distributes over a conjunction, so each Condition is necessary in its own right — and each under the same de dicto, structural-role scope just fixed. The joint result therefore carries three named consequences:

::: {.corollary}
**Necessity of Each Condition** · **R6** · *Result of R5*

Since □(T∧S∧Φ) is equivalent to □T ∧ □S ∧ □Φ (necessity distributes over conjunction):

- **Necessity of Temporality.** Temporality is instantiated in every possible world. □T.
- **Necessity of Spatiality.** Spatiality is instantiated in every possible world. □S.
- **Necessity of Physicality.** Physicality is instantiated in every possible world. □Φ.

Each follows as a conjunct of the Triconditional Necessity above. The Parasitic Negation arguments at §[§2.4.6](the-argument.html#sec-2-4-6)–2.4.8 supply narrower onset closures: they challenge emergence of a Condition from its own absence, but do not independently establish world-wise necessity.


:::

## 2.6 Triconditionality of Nature {#sec-2-6}

Time, Space, and Substance can look like three separate ingredients that happen to travel together. This section tests their unity under three readings: possibility, cross-entailment, and being. The unity claim is strongest within the realizer-level structure of genuine change, where full Condition-instantiation along any one axis co-instantiates the others. It is not the unrestricted claim that every abstract order, geometry, or bearer already instantiates all three.

The Structural Requirement ([§2.4](the-argument.html#sec-2-4)) identified the modal constraint with T∧S∧Φ. The biconditional ◇C ↔ T∧S∧Φ ([§2.6.10](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-10)) is one structural fact, not two. It is **identity**, not mere co-extension, with three readings (the Modal Identity, the Triconditional Cross-Entailment, the Ontological Identity) that pick out the same Nature from three different sides.

The identity claim is not licensed by biconditional form alone. Necessary co-extension between two distinct structural facts would deliver a necessary biconditional without delivering identity. The licensing condition here is stronger: the two sides have no independent ground. The same structural condition that makes change possible is what T∧S∧Φ names; there is no further fact one side reports that the other does not. Where two descriptions pick out the same modal constraint with no remainder, the difference is not between two facts but between two readings of one fact: the identity is structural, not numerical.[^2-6-0-identity-scope]

This is what forecloses Humean recombination **within the change-realizer domain**. Recombination operates on distinct existences that can be varied independently. Where T, S, and Φ are the mutually implicating roles of one genuine change-realizer, deleting one does not leave a thinner change-realizer; it leaves a different kind of abstract structure. The theorem does not forbid recombination among contingent occupants or among thin abstract analogues. Lewis's mosaic deletes the connection and keeps the structure that the connection was; the Ontological Identity is why the deletion never takes. (Lewis's concrete-worlds variant of the move is met at [§4.4.1](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-4-1).)

*Temporal direction note.* The T pillar throughout this chapter (directed, causal-order succession) is B-series in McTaggart's terms: asymmetric causal ordering, not A-series becoming or a moving-now. Whether directed succession requires an irreducibly A-series component, and whether McTaggart's positive proposal (the C-series, a non-temporal structural ordering from which temporal appearance derives) captures what Temporality consists in without genuine temporal addition, are addressed at [§4.2.5](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-2-5) (McTaggart's unreality of time) and [§4.2.6](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-2-6) (block universe / B-theory).

*Notation.* Four formal shapes recur across this section's preview and should be kept distinct. The plain biconditional ◇C ↔ T∧S∧Φ ([§2.6.10](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-10)) is the structural fact change-possibility and the Conditions share: one fact read from two sides. The necessitated biconditional □(◇C ↔ T∧S∧Φ), the Modal Identity ([§2.6.6](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-6)), is that one structural fact holding under necessitation. The theorem-level identities N ↔ □(T∧S∧Φ), N ↔ □◇C, and □(T∧S∧Φ) ↔ □◇C identify Nature with the necessitated co-instantiation read along three sides: modal, nomological, ontological. The first form is a biconditional; the second is its necessitation; the third set are the chapter's central theorem read three ways.

In the theorem below, N abbreviates Nature: the necessary presence of Temporality, Spatiality, and Physicality.

::: {.theorem}
**Triconditional Identity** · **T5** · *Theorem 5*

Nature is the necessary co-instantiation: point at any of the three and you are pointing at the others. The joint is treated as the book's fundamental primitive: T∧S∧Φ is not derived from something more fundamental, though the four lines of [§2.4](the-argument.html#sec-2-4) give independent derivational paths to its identification. Whether □ itself is primitive ideology or derived (a consequence of structural incapacity rather than a primitive modal operator) is addressed at [§2.10](the-argument.html#sec-2-10). N ↔ □(T∧S∧Φ), N ↔ □◇C, □(T∧S∧Φ) ↔ □◇C. (T5, previewed from [§2.6.10](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-10))


:::

The Triconditional Identity is the formal spine of the *Necessity of Nature* ([§2.8](the-argument.html#sec-2-8)) and the foundation on which the Null State Preclusion and the Necessary Occupancy Result are built at [§2.8.6](the-argument.html#sec-2-8-6).

**Condition-Individuation** closes the section at [§2.6.11](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-11): an external methodological screen that explains why exactly three Conditions, not two or four. Condition-Individuation is methodological closure on the substantive work of [§2.6.1](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-1)–2.6.10.

**Conditioned-Nature** closes the section semantically at [§2.6.12](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-12): a reading of Theorem 5 into the genitive *the nature of X*, showing that the chapter title *The Necessity of Nature* and its reverse *the nature of necessity* refer to the same N. Conditioned-Nature is semantic closure on Theorem 5's identity, paired with the methodological closure on its count at [§2.6.11](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-11).

[^2-6-0-identity-scope]: The identity of Nature with the necessitated co-instantiation of the Conditions is metaphysical-structural: the same modal constraint picked out with no remainder by the two descriptions (change-possibility and T∧S∧Φ). It is not a claim about what remains ideally conceivable under a primary intension, and the Modal Identity that follows is secondary / metaphysical necessity: necessity in the real modal structure, not closure of primary conceivability or of what is epistemically open. The two-dimensional question whether the non-identity remains primarily conceivable even where the secondary identity holds is engaged at [§4.1.2](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-2).

### 2.6.1 Three Conditions, One Nature {#sec-2-6-1}

T, S, and Φ are not three independent conditions that happen to co-occur. They *are* one structure read along three axes, and each, fully unpacked, reveals the others as its own internal requirements rather than as external correlates.

**Structure.** *A structure is not a thing alongside the things it structures. It is the ordered set of relations, constraints, and roles by which anything is intelligible as a thing, field, event, or configuration at all. In this book, structure names Reality under its necessary ordering: Temporality, Spatiality, and Physicality together as the conditions any possible item must already exhibit to be anything determinate. Structure therefore does not exist instead of things, and it is not imposed on a prior unstructured stuff. It is what any existing thing must already have in order to exist as anything at all.*

Temporality is not a finite thing, Spatiality is not a locational thing, Physicality is not a material thing. They *are* what finite things, locational things, and material things *consist in*.

T, S, and Φ are introduced at [§1.4](groundwork.html#sec-1-4) and derived at §[§2.4.5](the-argument.html#sec-2-4-5)–2.4.10. If change is genuinely possible, the Conditions are already in play ([§2.4](the-argument.html#sec-2-4)); [§2.6](the-argument.html#sec-2-6) turns on the converse: if the Conditions are instantiated, change is possible.

The consequence is immediate: these are not three necessities that travel together. They *are* one necessity seen from three sides.[^2-6-1-three-conditions-one-nature-ch4]

*The realizer move.* Every relation this chapter names (directed succession, genuine distinctness, causal transmission, exclusive occupancy, persistence, identity through change) admits a thin reading on which it reduces to labeling, self-relation, or coordinate notation, and a real reading on which it requires structural machinery to distinguish it from its deflationary mimic.

The Conditions T, S, and Φ are the realizers of each other's real readings. To say T ↔ (S ∧ Φ) is to say: the real reading of directed succession requires both relational extension and persistent bearing, and the conjunction of those two requires directed succession. The same holds for S ↔ (T ∧ Φ) and Φ ↔ (T ∧ S). Three triconditionals, one move, pivoted on each of the three terms in turn.

Succession alone demands an interval to cross and a medium to carry it. Extension alone demands a direction and a being. Persistence alone demands a direction to persist through and an interval to persist across. Each Condition, attempted in isolation, summons the other two as what the attempt consists in.

The triconditionals yield the *Mutual Containment Result*, gathered formally at [§2.6.5](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-5): lacking any one Condition entails lacking all three.

The physical confirmations of these relations (relativistic spacetime unification, conservation laws, thermodynamic asymmetry) are addressed in Chapter 7 as empirical expressions of what is established analytically here.

*A clarification on idiom.* The thin/real reading distinction throughout this section tracks a structural-functional distinction (what directed succession *requires* as a structural matter), not a hyperintensional-essence distinction (what directed succession is in its essence prior to modality). 'Internal requirements' names structural co-requirements of the primitive modal field, not essence-prior real definitions in Fine's sense. Whether this structural-functional use of 'consists in' and 'requires' can be kept stable against Fine's pressure (that any such structural identity just is a real definition under a different label) is the question addressed at [§4.1.10](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-10).

First: whether succession can stand without extension.

[^2-6-1-three-conditions-one-nature-ch4]: The three-Conditions-one-Nature framing (that T, S, and Φ are one structural fact read along three axes rather than three independent conditions) is engaged in Chapter 4. The closest contemporary ally is structural realism (Ladyman & Ross, French), which nonetheless diverges on what the structure consists in ([§4.3.9](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-9)). Sider's structuralism ([§4.4.7](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-4-7)), bundle theory and tropes on the compose-by-relation picture ([§4.3.10](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-10)), and mereological nihilism on whether there is anything for the three to be conditions of ([§4.3.11](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-11)) press from their own directions, and Quine's anti-distinction pressure asks whether the three pivots name a single fact under three readings or three independent facts ([§4.1.6](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-6)).

### 2.6.2 Succession's Two Conditions {#sec-2-6-2}

*The realizer move, applied to T ↔ (S ∧ Φ).* Directed succession is biconditional with both relational extension and persistent bearing: T ↔ (S ∧ Φ). The realizer move runs across all three terms: each, taken in its real (not thin) reading, requires the others as what makes it real rather than notational. Four lines work the T↔S link explicitly (two in each direction, each refuting a distinct deflationary mimic), and each line already deploys Φ in the work that makes it run. The same four lines deliver T↔Φ: not as a separate step, but as what the lines are doing already. The realizer move is repeated from the extension and persistence pivots at §[§2.6.3](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-3) and 2.6.4; the result is cross-confirmation, not assembly. The succession pivot alone already delivers the full triconditional; the three vantages are gathered at [§2.6.5](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-5).

*Direction 1: T→S.* Two lines converge on the same result: directed succession analytically requires relational extension.

*First, directed succession is a reaching, and a reaching needs an interval to cross: that interval is relational extension (the traversability line).* A thin reading of directed succession: state A is followed by state B, full stop. But Temporality's Directionality ([§1.4](groundwork.html#sec-1-4)) has already built more into the relation: the after-state is not merely adjacent to the before-state but is reached by it, with the directional ordering itself traveling from one to the other. The travel here is not yet specifically Φ-causal transmission in the canonical event-to-event sense; that is delivered under its full physical reading at [§2.6.4](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-4) and [§2.4.8](the-argument.html#sec-2-4-8). The travel at the level of this line is the operative work that distinguishes a real reaching from a notational adjacency. The line does not assume Φ as a separate premise; it surfaces Φ as already engaged in the work T requires to be more than notation. Travel of this kind still requires a medium to travel through. Directed succession with no interval between its states is not directed succession with unusual spatial properties; it is bare replacement under a different name. If the directional reaching genuinely runs from A to B, it must cross something. If it crosses nothing, it is not traveling but replacing. The interval it crosses is relational extension.

*Second, the before-and-after asymmetry has nowhere to reside but the relation between the relata, and that relation is extension (the asymmetry-location line).* A thinner reading: A and B are distinct and A is before B, but the asymmetry is primitive, with nothing to ground it. Ask where the asymmetry resides. Not in A alone (A does not contain the fact that B comes after it). Not in B alone (the mirror problem). Not in a third state floating free (that would need its own grounding). The only remaining location is the relation between them, and a relation with structurally differentiated positions between distinct relata is relational extension. The Bateson [-@bateson1972] gloss lands in the same place: the causal imprint the after-state carries is a difference that makes a difference, and a difference that makes a difference requires a structure of alternatives among which the signal selected. A structure of alternatives is relational extension.

By PII (the Principle of Identity of Indiscernibles), relata with no relational structure and identical intrinsic properties are one relatum, not two; relata with no relational structure but distinct intrinsic properties are distinguishable but unordered: nothing makes one *after* the other. Directed succession specifically requires a relational carrier for the direction. That carrier is extension.

PII is contested. Black [-@black1952] offers the standard two-spheres counterexample: two qualitatively identical iron spheres in an otherwise empty universe, distinct individuals despite intrinsic indiscernibility. The line's PII appeal does not require strong PII (individuation by intrinsic properties alone). It requires only the weaker claim that *relata in directed succession* require relational structure to ground their ordering. Black's spheres themselves stand in a relational structure (each at some distance from the other) which is the kind of structure the line invokes. The line's PII reading is the relational one, which survives Black; strong intrinsic PII is not needed for the line to deliver.

*Direction 2: S→T.* Two lines converge from the other direction: relational extension analytically requires directed succession.

*First, a real interval is one that can be crossed, and a crossing is directed succession (the interval-reality line).* A thin reading of relational extension: positions separated by intervals. But an interval that nothing could cross is not a distance; it is notation. The reality of an interval (what distinguishes a real extended structure from a coordinate labeling) is its traversability. Traversability is directed succession: a crossing is influence moving from one position to another in ordered fashion. Strip out succession and the *interval* loses the feature that made it real rather than notational.

*Second, distinct positions are distinct only by sustaining “at x, then at y,” and that takes directed succession (the position-individuation line).* A thinner reading: positions are distinct by stipulation; nothing further grounds their separation. Ask what makes position x not identical to position y if nothing could distinguish them by occupying them differently. The answer cannot be intrinsic properties of positions, and whether one takes a relationalist line (positions have no intrinsic properties apart from their relational structure) or a substantivalist line (positions have an intrinsic identity, but that identity does no individuating work without the relational structure that ties it to the rest of the manifold), the individuation of x from y must run through how they stand to one another rather than through any content that distinguishes them independently. The answer must be that the positions sustain distinct possibilities: something could be at x without being at y, and could move between them. Sustaining distinct possibilities requires directed succession as the structure within which *at x then at y* has content. Without succession, the *distinctness* of positions collapses into labels that differ in no operative way.

Which line bears the most weight depends on what the reader resists. The traversability and interval-reality lines are decisive for anyone who grants that real structure must be operative rather than notational. The asymmetry-location and position-individuation lines are decisive for anyone who grants the relata but resists the realizer: they close the remaining gap by locating where the contested feature must reside.

What about sequences that are not spatial, or structures without time? Three stock objections press: primitive thisness (states individuated with no relational structure); primitive asymmetric dependence (the after-state depends on the before-state with nothing between); *non-spatial* sequences (order without extension). None blocks the result. If states are genuinely distinct, that distinctness consists in more than two labels that fail to match. If a *sequence* is only logical order (the natural numbers under <, say, or Prior's [-@prior1967] tense-logic operators), Temporality in the operative sense has not yet arrived; what has arrived is a formalism whose propositional relata are ordered by logical operations, itself a relationally extended abstract structure.

The fuller tests belong with [§4.2.4](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-2-4), where four Platonist positions (Frege-Gödel classical Platonism, Shapiro's *ante rem* structuralism, Maddy's naturalized Platonism, and Balaguer's plenitudinous Platonism) are put under load individually, and where Benacerraf's [-@benacerraf1965; -@benacerraf1973] multiple-reduction and access results close the residue.

*Scope.* The extension required here is not necessarily physical space in the recognizably Newtonian sense; the succession required is not necessarily physical time. Each is the structural condition of which physical space and physical time are this universe's realizers. The claim is framework-invariant: any medium hosting causally structured succession must exhibit relational extension, and any medium hosting real relational extension must exhibit directed succession. Physical spacetime realizes both. Nothing in the argument restricts the realization to that case.

*Lifting to the triconditional.* Each of the four lines argues T↔S, but each line already deploys Φ in its argument: Φ appears not as a separate premise but as part of the operative work T↔S requires to run. The traversability line invokes travel; travel requires a traveler that persists across the crossing (Φ). The interval-reality line invokes traversal across the interval; traversal requires the same. The asymmetry-location line invokes the asymmetry being carried forward by the after-state; that carrying-forward requires Φ-persistence. The position-individuation line invokes positions sustaining distinct possibilities across the succession that makes them distinct possibilities; the sustaining is Φ at the level of position-bearing.

The reverse direction runs the same way. A Φ-persistent being with no Temporality has no succession to persist through; a Φ-medium with no S has no positions to bear; a Φ-relation between cause and effect requires direction (T) and interval (S) to be more than self-relation. The four lines therefore deliver Φ↔T alongside T↔S, as part of the same realizer move read from the T pivot.

The pairwise biconditional T↔S arrives already engaging Φ; the same lines deliver T↔Φ; the cross-entailment Φ↔S follows from the symmetric work from the S pivot established at [§2.6.3](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-3). The result is T ↔ (S ∧ Φ): succession cannot stand without both extension and being, and the conjunction cannot stand without succession.

*Duration* presents as temporal vocabulary: the span of an interval. But the result reached above runs in ordinary language before any formal analysis arrives. Duration requires a persistent being (Φ): without something that endures, there is no duration *of* anything, only a labeled interval with no occupant. It requires relational extension (S): without somewhere for the being to be, the interval cannot be located, and an interval without location is not a span but a label. Strip either Condition and the word stops applying. Duration is not a temporal word that happens to imply the others. It is a triconditional word built around the succession pivot: T ↔ (S ∧ Φ) embedded in a single noun.

*What converges.* Four lines, one move, three Conditions. Succession cannot occur without extension to cross, an interval cannot be real without something to cross it, and what crosses must persist to do so.[^2-6-2-succession-pivot-ch4] Three sides of one structural fact: the realizer move read from the succession pivot, with the same fact read from the extension and persistence pivots at §[§2.6.3](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-3)–2.6.4.

[^2-6-2-succession-pivot-ch4]: The T pivot, T ↔ (S ∧ Φ) and the four realizer lines (traversability, asymmetry-location, interval-reality, position-individuation), is engaged in Chapter 4. The canonical opponent of the realizer move's real reading is the Humean denial of necessary connection between distinct existences ([§4.1.4](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-4)). Sider's stage theory and temporal-parts ontology press on what makes succession real ([§4.2.8](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-2-8)), Platonism about non-spatial sequences (Frege–Gödel, Shapiro, Maddy, Balaguer) is the principal order-without-extension opponent ([§4.2.4](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-2-4)), emergent time presses on whether T is fundamental enough to enter the biconditional ([§4.2.3](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-2-3)), and Tegmark's mathematical universe asks whether order-without-extension is enough ([§4.3.7](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-7)).

### 2.6.3 Extension's Two Conditions {#sec-2-6-3}

*The realizer move, applied to S ↔ (T ∧ Φ).* Real relational extension is biconditional with both directed succession and persistent bearing: S ↔ (T ∧ Φ). If positions are real, something must occupy them, something must distinguish them through ordered relation, and crossings between them must run in time. Four lines work the S↔Φ link explicitly (two in each direction, each refuting a distinct deflationary mimic), and each line already deploys T in the work that makes it run. The same four lines deliver S↔T: not as a separate step, but as what the lines are doing already. The same realizer move is worked from the succession and persistence pivots at §[§2.6.2](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-2) and 2.6.4; the result is cross-confirmation, not assembly. The extension pivot alone already delivers the full triconditional; the three vantages are gathered at [§2.6.5](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-5).

*Direction 1: Φ→S.* Two lines converge on the same result: Physicality analytically requires Spatiality.

*First, the distinctness line.* For causation to be real, its source and uptake terms must be genuinely distinguishable, not merely two names for one undifferentiated state. This need not require two numerically distinct beings: one persisting system may occupy the causal roles at different stages. Intrinsic difference alone is not enough to order those roles. For the causal terms to be structurally distinct, they must occupy distinguishable positions or states within a relational structure. That is the Spatiality-role of relational differentiation. The constitutive claim (that the genuine non-identity of causal relata is relational non-identity) receives the haecceitist's primitive-thisness counter (set out at strength in [§2.4.7](the-argument.html#sec-2-4-7)) in the same form, and survives by the same articulability bridge. Even a primitive haecceity that distinguishes one causal relatum from another must remain articulable as *this-cause* rather than *that-effect* in the very specification of what it distinguishes. A haecceity that distinguishes one causal relatum from another is itself a relation between the haecceity and what it is the haecceity of, and the *this-cause / that-effect* contrast that haecceities pick out is the very relational non-identity Spatiality names, carried at the level of the thisness rather than at the level of qualitative properties. Haecceitism about causal relata either reads relational structure into its haecceities (confirming Spatiality's contribution under different vocabulary) or strips it out and loses the explanatory work the haecceities were posited to do.

*Second, the interaction line.* Causal exchange is not a bare relation between two labels. It requires transmission from a source-state or role to an uptake-state or role. The interval need not be a distance between two beings; internal causation may run between distinguishable states of one persisting system. What cannot be removed is relational separation between the causal terms: without any distinction between source and uptake, there is no path or articulation by which influence could run, only one undifferentiated event described twice. The relational interval that distinguishes the causal terms is the Spatiality-role invoked here.

Whether one approaches from the distinctness of the relata or from the interaction between them, Physicality without Spatiality collapses: either the relata are not genuinely distinct, or the causation has no path. A being that carries influence needs somewhere to carry it. The interval does not merely lie between them; it is what makes them two things at all.

*Direction 2: S→Φ.* Now the reverse. Two lines converge from the other direction: Spatiality analytically requires Physicality.

*First, the occupancy line.* Spatiality's defining structural feature is exclusive occupancy: the fact that two things cannot occupy the same position. But exclusion is a causal act in the broad sense: to exclude is to prevent, to resist, to block, and preventing, resisting, and blocking are things only a causally active medium can do. A primitivist about exclusion who reads exclusion as a primitive structural fact rather than a canonical-causal one inherits the same medium-work under different vocabulary, by the argument of [§2.4.8](the-argument.html#sec-2-4-8): whatever makes a primitive exclusion *do* exclusion-work must operate across the foreclosure interval, and that cross-interval operation is what Φ names, whether read as canonical causation or as primitive foreclosure performing the same structural function.

A position that nothing *could* occupy is not a spatial position; it is an abstract coordinate label. The reality of spatial positions (what makes them positions rather than mathematical indices) is that they are occupiable. The argument does not deny that *empty* regions of physical space are real: empty regions are real precisely because they are occupiable; something *could* occupy them, even when nothing currently does. The reality of an empty region rests on the occupiability of its positions, not on the presence of actual occupants at every position. What collapses into a coordinate label is not the empty region but the would-be position that nothing could ever occupy. And occupiability requires something capable of occupying: a medium with the causal capacity to occupy and to exclude other occupants. That medium is Physicality. Exclusive occupancy without a being is exclusion with nothing doing the excluding.

*Second, the interval line.* A relational interval between two positions is real only if something can traverse it. An interval that nothing crosses, nothing bridges, nothing moves through is not a distance; it is a notation. The reality of the interval consists in its traversability, and traversability requires a medium that persists through the crossing. The medium that makes spatial intervals real rather than abstract (by being what crosses them and persists through them) is Physicality.

Whether one approaches from the occupancy of positions or from the reality of intervals, Spatiality without Physicality collapses: either exclusion has no excluder, or intervals have no medium to make them real. The pressure is symmetric: just as Physicality without Spatiality had no path for its causation, Spatiality without Physicality has no medium to make its positions real. Each is the other's internal requirement, not its external correlate.

*Lifting to the triconditional.* Each of the four lines runs on more than the pair it names. Causal exchange (the interaction line) requires transmission, and transmission across an interval is travel, already temporal. Exclusive occupancy (the occupancy line) is exclusion, and exclusion is a causal act that runs in time. Distinctness (the distinctness line) presupposes positions whose differentiation cannot be static: a being that excludes another at a position must endure long enough to do so. The pairwise biconditional S↔Φ arrives already engaging T; the four lines deliver S↔T as part of the same argument. The result is S ↔ (T ∧ Φ): extension cannot stand without both succession and being, and the conjunction cannot stand without extension.

*Movement* presents as spatial vocabulary: traversal of distance. But the result reached above runs in ordinary language before any formal analysis arrives. Movement requires directed succession (T): without before and after, there is no moving, only occupying: being at a position rather than arriving at it. It requires a persistent being (Φ): without something that moves, there is no movement, only position change: a difference between two states with no owner of the difference. Strip either Condition and the word stops applying. Movement is not a spatial word that happens to imply the others. It is a triconditional word built around the extension pivot: S ↔ (T ∧ Φ) embedded in a single noun.

*What converges.* Extension without a being is empty. A being without extension has no positions to occupy. Neither has its work to do without succession to do it through. Three sides of one structural fact: the same fact read from the extension pivot. The remaining link is the one that feels obvious, which is precisely why it must be proved.[^2-6-3-extension-pivot-ch4]

[^2-6-3-extension-pivot-ch4]: The S pivot, S ↔ (T ∧ Φ) and the four realizer lines (distinctness, interaction, occupancy, interval), is engaged in Chapter 4. The canonical anti-S opponent is mereological nihilism: no composites, hence no relational structure beyond simples ([§4.3.11](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-11)). Structural realism (Ladyman, French) is the closest ally on relational fabric, diverging on what the relations consist in ([§4.3.9](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-9)), Sider's structuralism takes up spatial structure ([§4.4.7](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-4-7)), bundle theory and tropes ask whether positions are anything beyond their occupants ([§4.3.10](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-10)), and Tegmark asks whether relational extension is mathematical rather than substantive ([§4.3.7](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-7)).

### 2.6.4 Persistence's Two Conditions {#sec-2-6-4}

*The realizer move, applied to Φ ↔ (T ∧ S).* Persistent bearing is biconditional with both directed succession and relational extension: Φ ↔ (T ∧ S). If something persists, it persists through temporal order as a bearer situated within relational structure; it need not move across a spatial distance. If directed succession and real relational differentiation are instantiated, the argument asks what bears them. Four lines work the T↔Φ link explicitly (two in each direction, each refuting a distinct deflationary mimic), and each line already deploys S in the work that makes it run. The same four lines deliver S↔Φ: not as a separate step, but as what the lines are doing already. The same realizer move is worked from the succession and extension pivots at §[§2.6.2](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-2) and 2.6.3; the result is cross-confirmation, not assembly. The mimics on each side must be refuted explicitly.

*Direction 1: T→Φ.* Two lines converge on the same result: Temporality analytically requires Physicality.

*First, the continuity line.* Think of a relay race. The baton must be carried from one runner to the next: if it vanishes at the handoff and a new baton appears, nothing was relayed. Directed succession works the same way: something must carry influence from before-state to after-state. Without a persistence medium, what produced the before-state leaves nothing behind, and the after-state arrives from nowhere. That is not directed transition. It is replacement. The distinction between transition and replacement is not a matter of degree. It is constitutive. A before-state that transmits nothing forward does not produce an after-state. For succession to be causally structured rather than merely sequential, something must persist across the transition as the vehicle of causal transmission. That persistence medium is Physicality.

*Second, the identity line.* For there to be a subject that changes, something must persist as the same subject through the change. If nothing endures from the before-state into the after-state, there is no subject that underwent the transition; there are two disconnected states with nothing in common. Change requires a thing that was one way and is now another. Remove the thing and you remove the change: what remains is two descriptions with no owner.

Whether one approaches from the continuity of causal influence or from the identity of the changing subject, Temporality without Physicality collapses: either succession has no vehicle, or change has no subject. Persistence is not what survives change. It is what makes change possible: the invariant through which variation has content. Something that cannot stay is not passing through time. It is flashing and vanishing. That is replacement, not succession.

*Direction 2: Φ→T.* Two lines converge from the other direction: Physicality analytically requires Temporality.

*First, the persistence line.* Persistence is not a static property. It is persistence through: through transitions, through changes, through the passage from before to after. A medium that never stands in an earlier/later order is not persisting through anything. It exists at no moment, endures across no interval, and sustains nothing from one state to the next. To persist is to be the same thing at a later time as at an earlier time. Remove the temporal ordering and there is nothing for persistence to consist in. Physicality without Temporality is not a being in a reduced mode. It is the word *being* with no structural content.

*Second, the causation line.* Causal capacity (the ability to affect and be affected) requires asymmetric ordering. The cause precedes the effect. The affecting comes before the being-affected. Without temporal direction, there is no fact distinguishing which is the cause and which is the effect. The causal relation becomes symmetric, and symmetric causation is not causation but mere correlation. The asymmetry is not a feature added to causation from outside. It is what causation consists in: an influence that runs from source to recipient, not a symmetric correlation between co-occurring states. Remove the temporal direction and the influence has no arrow, and an arrow without direction is not an arrow.
