Whether one approaches from the persistence of the medium or from the directionality of its causal relations, Physicality without Temporality collapses: either persistence has no succession to persist through, or causation has no direction.

Succession needs a persistence medium. The persistence medium needs temporal direction. They empty together. The argument that derived them ran on both.

*Lifting to the triconditional.* Each of the four lines argues T↔Φ, but each already deploys S in its argument: a baton must be carried across (the continuity line: carrying happens between positions); the subject that endures must endure somewhere (the identity line: there is no placeless subject); causation runs from one position to another (the causation line: the asymmetry of cause-to-effect is asymmetry across positions); persistence persists through an interval (the persistence line: the very phrase requires extension). Strip S from any of these and the line loses what makes it run. The pairwise biconditional T↔Φ arrives already engaging S; that S-deployment delivers half of S↔Φ (Φ→S: any argument that yields Φ here passes through S, so Φ-instantiation requires S-instantiation). The other half (S→Φ) is delivered by triangulation with §[§2.6.2](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-2) and [§2.6.3](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-3): T↔(S∧Φ) is given at [§2.6.2](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-2) and S↔(T∧Φ) at [§2.6.3](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-3); the three biconditionals jointly entail Φ↔(T∧S). The four lines here do not need to derive S↔Φ in isolation; they need only deliver T↔Φ in a way that already engages S, which they do, and Φ↔(T∧S) is jointly delivered by triangulation across all three pivots at §[§2.6.2](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-2)–2.6.4. The result is Φ ↔ (T ∧ S): persistent bearing cannot stand without both succession and extension, and the conjunction cannot stand without a being.

*Interaction* presents as causal vocabulary: things affecting one another. But the result reached above runs in ordinary language before any formal analysis arrives. Interaction requires relational extension (S): without distinct positions, there is no between, and without a between, what appears to be exchange is a single event described twice. It requires directed succession (T): causal influence runs from before-state to after-state; without that direction, what appears to be affecting is correlation, not causation. Strip either Condition and the word stops applying. Interaction is not a causal word that happens to imply the others. It is a triconditional word built around the persistence pivot: Φ ↔ (T ∧ S) embedded in a single noun.

*A dynamic supplement.* The realizer lines establish Φ↔(T∧S) conceptually: persistence cannot stand without succession and extension, and the conjunction cannot stand without a being. That derivation is the load-bearing argument for the biconditional; what follows is characterization of Φ's further texture, not additional derivation. The same persistence is available as first-person datum, and three further observations sharpen what kind of host Φ is.

*Persistence hosts change.* A thought held in attention spans changes that proceed around it: the room's air exchanging, the page's light scattering, the body's blood circulating. The thought spans the changes; the changes do not erase it. This does not require an unchanged host. A process may alter its own bearer while enough continuity remains to carry the process and its effects. Φ is the bearing continuity through which change occurs, not an invariant configuration that change can never affect.

*Persistence admits hold-and-proceed.* Breath suspended, heartbeat continuing, neural firing continuing, manuscript resting on the desk: one change-process is held while sibling processes proceed at their own rates. The temporal order of change is not totally serial. There is no master succession running the world with everything else as derived sub-steps. Φ is the condition under which many change-processes can run concurrently and one can be suspended without arresting the others.

*Persistence is grain-independent: it admits processes at different temporal grains.* A held thought spanning an interval and blinks occurring periodically across the same interval are persistence-bearing processes at different temporal grains within the same Φ. The observation is not that the cadences are mathematically incommensurable, but that no master cadence is given in the data as constitutively fixing both. Their temporal relation is contingent; their co-occurrence within one persistence-bearing structure is the point. Φ is the condition under which processes at different grains are co-hosted at all.

*What the supplement adds.* The realizer lines establish Φ↔(T∧S); these three observations characterize what Φ further is. Φ is hosting, plural, and grain-independent: a host that change operates within rather than upon, a manifold that admits concurrent suspension, a condition that does not impose a master cadence on what it hosts. *Cogito ergo muto* ([§2.8.2](the-argument.html#sec-2-8-2)) catches the denier of change at the token level; the supplement characterizes what the catch is catching the denier inside of. The denial is hosted, runs alongside sibling processes, and proceeds at a cadence the denier did not select.

*Where the three triconditionals stand.* Each pivot has been worked in both directions: T ↔ (S ∧ Φ) in [§2.6.2](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-2), S ↔ (T ∧ Φ) in [§2.6.3](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-3), Φ ↔ (T ∧ S) here. Three pivots on one fact, twelve lines in total, every pair of Conditions covered twice from the vantage of each pivot. The full instantiation of any one Condition, when unpacked, reveals the other two as internal requirements rather than external correlates.

*What converges.* Three Conditions, three triconditionals, and one structure read through all three. What that structure amounts to (as one fact rather than three) is what follows.[^2-6-4-persistence-pivot-ch4]

[^2-6-4-persistence-pivot-ch4]: The Φ pivot, Φ ↔ (T ∧ S) and the four realizer lines (continuity, identity, persistence, causation), plus the hosting/plural/grain-independent supplement, is engaged in Chapter 4. The strongest opponent of the identity line is eliminativism and illusionism about persistence ([§4.3.2](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-2)). Sider's stage theory reads persistence as concatenation of stages rather than endurance ([§4.2.8](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-2-8)), bundle theory and tropes ask whether there is a persistent subject beyond the bundle ([§4.3.10](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-10)), idealism accepts persistence but reads it as mental rather than as Φ ([§4.3.5](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-5)), Russellian monism posits intrinsic categorical natures behind the persistence-medium ([§4.3.3](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-3)), and the Humean denial of necessary connection presses at the persistence-vehicle for causal transmission ([§4.1.4](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-4)).

### 2.6.5 Mutual Containment {#sec-2-6-5}

The three pivot derivations of §[§2.6.2](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-2)–2.6.4 are now in hand, and they compress into a single result:

::: {.corollary}
**Mutual Containment** · **R7** · *Result of §[§2.6.2](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-2)–2.6.4*

The three relations jointly establish that T, S, and Φ are not three independently defined Conditions that happen to require each other. Each Condition, when its definition is unpacked to its full logical content, reveals the other two as internal requirements rather than external correlates. Temporality's genuine state-distinctness requires Spatiality's relational structure. Spatiality's exclusive occupiability requires Physicality's causal capacity, because exclusive occupancy just is causal exclusion, and causal exclusion requires a medium that can act. Physicality's causal persistence requires Temporality's temporal succession. The mutual entailment is complete, symmetric, and analytic, derivable from the definitions alone without appeal to empirical facts about our universe.


:::

The entailment claimed is not that T, S, and Φ happen to co-occur with metaphysical necessity, as though they were three independent features that every possible world happens to contain. It is the result of the realizer move worked three times in the three pivot derivations: the full logical content of each Condition's definition, when unpacked, contains the other two as internal requirements. The Mutual Containment Result inherits directly from the three pivot derivations: T↔(S∧Φ) at [§2.6.2](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-2), S↔(T∧Φ) at [§2.6.3](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-3), and Φ↔(T∧S) at [§2.6.4](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-4), each pivot supplying one of the three bilateral entailments; the present result compresses them into the joint claim. The convergent lines of §[§2.6.2](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-2)–2.6.4 are demonstrations of definitional containment, not inductive observations of co-occurrence, and they are demonstrations of a single move read from three pivots, not three independent arguments that happen to compose.

The distinction matters: co-occurrence would leave the Conditions separable in principle even if inseparable in fact. Containment makes the separation incoherent, not as a feature of which worlds exist, but as a constraint on what *world* consists in.

A causal power with no position has nothing to act on and nothing it acts from; a position with no persistence is no one's position, because nothing is there long enough to be somewhere; persistence with no succession is a state that never transitions: all of the subject, at once, nothing changed. Each role, taken by itself, is trying to describe something only the other two make describable. Mutual definitional containment, stripped of its vocabulary, is the claim that a thing is the three roles working at once, or it is nothing at all.

What happens if one Condition is removed? Remove Physicality and ask what is changing: without a being, succession indexes nothing and extension contains nothing; the grammar of change survives, but the semantics do not. Remove Spatiality and ask where it is changing: Physicality flickers through states with no field of realization, a subject with a clock but nowhere to put it. Remove Temporality and ask when it is changing: Physicality extends through space in frozen diversity, difference without succession, a snapshot with no before or after. Each removal does not weaken Reality; it collapses it. The incoherence of that collapse is developed in [§2.7](the-argument.html#sec-2-7).

*The physics-register line.* The mutual entailment also receives confirmation from inside physics. @noether1918 established that every continuous symmetry of a physical system corresponds to a conservation law: symmetry in Temporality yields energy conservation, symmetry in Spatiality yields momentum conservation. Each conservation law is a statement about what persists across transformation: Φ, named in the vocabulary of physics. Within Lagrangian dynamics, T and S as continuous symmetries entail Φ as a conservation consequence. The line is confirmation rather than independent derivation: it presupposes the action principle and the Lagrangian framework that licenses the symmetry-to-conservation move, both of which are results within physical theory rather than premises of the present argument. The biconditional is derived from inside logic (the three preceding lines); Noether confirms it from inside physics. The conservation line is developed at full length at [§7.5.3](nature-alone.html#sec-7-5-3).

Every step of any derivation moves from one state to the next, an ordering that cannot be reversed without losing the argument. Every proposition occupies a position the preceding one did not, a distinction inference requires to advance. Across those steps something must persist, a medium that holds derivation taut across all three coordinates. Inference does not describe the Triconditional Cross-Entailment; it instantiates it. A directed succession of thoughts, through a manifold of distinct propositions, sustained by a medium that persists from premise to conclusion, is not a description of the structure but an instance of it.

One structural fact, read from three directions. The next section delivers it as the Modal Identity, the biconditional that combines the Structural Requirement, P3 (§[§2.4.5](the-argument.html#sec-2-4-5)–2.4.9), and the converse ([§2.4.10](the-argument.html#sec-2-4-10)). The Modal Identity and the Ontological Identity (§[§2.6.6](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-6), 2.6.8) do not add a new structure on top of that result; they name the one this derivation has already forced.[^2-6-5-co-instantiation-ch4]

[^2-6-5-co-instantiation-ch4]: The objections to the Mutual Containment claim (the denial that T, S, and Φ are independently separable) are engaged in Chapter 4: bundle theory and tropes, which deny compositional unity ([§4.3.10](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-10)), mereological nihilism, which denies that any joint instantiation runs deeper than the simples ([§4.3.11](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-11)), Sider's structuralism ([§4.4.7](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-4-7)), and structural realism ([§4.3.9](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-9)).

### 2.6.6 Modal Identity {#sec-2-6-6}

This is the first of three readings of the Triconditional Identity ([§2.6.10](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-10)): Nature read from the side of possibility, the reading from which ◇C points at the structure. The Modal Identity, the Triconditional Cross-Entailment, and the Ontological Identity each show the same inseparability of T, S, and Φ from a different side. Each is given as a reading because at every viewpoint the biconditional is not two facts requiring each other but one structural fact under one of three readings: modal from the side of possibility, nomological from the cross-entailment among the roles, ontological from the side of being.

The Modal Identity concerns the full Conditions where they function as a genuine change-realizer. Its modal force is not an unrestricted claim that every abstract order, geometry, or bearer instantiates all three. It is the claim that any world in the fixed global domain W that realizes change realizes the mutually implicating T, S, and Φ structure, and that the canonical derivation establishes those Conditions throughout W. The Modal Identity reads the joint structural result from the side of change-possibility rather than reducing it to a feature of modal vocabulary.

The main conclusion, □(T∧S∧Φ), is already in hand from the chain closed at [§2.5](the-argument.html#sec-2-5) (declared formally as Theorem 6, the Necessity of Nature, at [§2.8.5](the-argument.html#sec-2-8-5)): the forward conditional ◇C → T∧S∧Φ ([§2.4.5](the-argument.html#sec-2-4-5)–2.4.9), its necessitation ([§2.4.9](the-argument.html#sec-2-4-9)), the necessary modal constraint □◇C ([§2.3](the-argument.html#sec-2-3)), and the bilateral witnesses ◇C ([§2.2](the-argument.html#sec-2-2)). The converse (T∧S∧Φ → ◇C) at [§2.4.10](the-argument.html#sec-2-4-10) and the identity reading developed here are successively stronger claims, each doing work beyond what the proof to the main conclusion requires.

The forward conditional alone delivers the conclusion. The forward conditional together with the converse (as the biconditional) forecloses the frozen-structure scenario, required for the account of what structure actually does. The identity (reading the biconditional as a single structural fact rather than two conditionals) delivers the ground beneath both, and grounds the ontological reading carried forward at [§2.8.5](the-argument.html#sec-2-8-5) and in Chapter 3, though the derivations there do not themselves require it.

A reader who grants only the forward conditional has the proof. A reader who grants the converse as well (the full biconditional) has the metaphysical picture. A reader who grants the identity has the ontology.

A reader who accepts the biconditional but resists the identity claim still has the conclusion. What they do not have is the ground beneath the argument that follows. If the possibility of change and the structure of Reality are merely two facts that require each other in every possible world, then a world without the structure of Reality is a world where change is impossible, but it remains, formally, a description of a possible world with unusual properties.

The identity claim closes this: if the two are one structural fact, then a world without the structure of Reality is not a sparse world. It is the absence of what worlds are made of.

The generic-identity reading is available only at the specified resolution. Its inheritance chain runs through [§2.4.10](the-argument.html#sec-2-4-10) (the converse from the full Conditions to ◇C) and §[§2.6.2](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-2)–2.6.5 (the cross-axis relations inside a genuine change-realizer). The argument does not identify every thin abstract analogue of order, difference, or bearing with the full Conditions.

Each step in the chain rules out a specific candidate for independent specification: structure-without-change-possibility is foreclosed at [§2.4.10](the-argument.html#sec-2-4-10); change-possibility-without-structure is foreclosed across each axis individually at §[§2.6.2](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-2)–2.6.5. The independence that the identity claim denies is the very thing the upstream chain has already foreclosed.

Try to specify the Conditions without invoking change-possibility. Temporality is causally structured succession, Spatiality is relational extension, Physicality is causal persistence. Each *is* what change *consists in* from a different direction. Every specification of the Conditions already invokes change-possibility as its content.

Now try the reverse. Specify change without the Conditions. Change requires a before and after: Temporality. Distinct positions: Spatiality. A medium that carries influence: Physicality. The independent description is not available in either direction.

Consider the attempt. Think of change without a before and after, without distinct positions, without a medium. The thought does not arrive at an impoverished version of change. It does not arrive at all, because arriving is change, and you have just invoked all three in the act of trying to think without them.

These exercises illustrate the foreclosure rather than establish it: the no-surplus result is fixed by the role-definitions of §[§1.3](groundwork.html#sec-1-3)–1.4 together with the converse at [§2.4.10](the-argument.html#sec-2-4-10); the operative instantiation of the Conditions just *is* the availability of change. The inability to think the one without the other is the symptom of that structural identity, not its ground; nothing in the claim rests on what can or cannot be conceived.

This is not Kripke's water-and-H₂O identity. It shares the analytic-identity form Kripke himself distinguishes from mere necessary biconditional, but operates at the structural level where the surface/essence seam he exploits does not open. The contrast is handled directly at [§4.1.1](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-1) and [§4.1.2](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-2). Here it suffices that the biconditional does not hold because two independent facts require each other. It holds because the independence was never there.

The hardest pressure on the identity reading comes from the B-theoretic block. A four-dimensional manifold in which all events stand in tenseless earlier-than relations has, on the standard analytic reading, T (the temporal ordering), S (the spatial extension), and Φ (whatever fills it) all instantiated, yet nothing on the picture succeeds, nothing yields, nothing carries forward. Every event is just there.

The B-theorist will press: this is structure without change-as-becoming. The Conditions and change-possibility, on this scenario, come apart at exactly the seam the identity reading was supposed to seal.

The full engagement belongs to [§4.2.6](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-2-6), where the perspectival-versus-structural-becoming distinction is taken up in full along with the further questions (the phenomenology of becoming, presentism-versus-eternalism, and growing-block alternatives); here only the narrower point needs to land for the Modal Identity — that tenseless ordering meets the specification of Temporality at [§1.4](groundwork.html#sec-1-4).

Does tenseless ordering count as Temporality in the sense the Conditions invoke? That is the whole of the pressure, and the structural answer is yes.

Temporality as defined at [§1.4](groundwork.html#sec-1-4) is succession with duration, direction, and causal weight, and the B-theoretic ordering relation is exactly that, viewed from outside the block rather than from within it. From no point inside the block does succession fail to obtain; from every point, the ordering is precisely the before-and-after the Conditions name.

What the B-theorist's static description subtracts is the perspective from within (the experience of becoming), and the experience of becoming is not what the Conditions consist in. The Conditions are the structural shape that makes both the within-perspective and the without-perspective coherent descriptions of the same Nature.

Take the block reading and the identity holds: structure *is* what change-possibility *consists in*, viewed from outside; change-possibility *is* what structure does, viewed from inside. The B-theorist who rejects change-as-becoming has not separated the Conditions from change-possibility; they have specified change-possibility at the level the block describes. The identity survives the deflation.

Fine's asymmetry (essential to {Socrates} that it contains Socrates, but not essential to Socrates that he belong to {Socrates}) has no purchase here. That asymmetry requires two entities with distinct essential profiles. The Conditions and change are not two entities. They *are* one structural requirement, and the asymmetry needs two distinct things where there is only one.

And the warrant for the identity is not that the two hold across the same worlds. What makes Fine's {Socrates} an asymmetry is individuating surplus: the set essentially contains Socrates, while Socrates bears no essential tie to the set, so one side carries content the other lacks.

Between the Conditions and change-possibility there is no such surplus in either direction: every specification of the one is already a specification of the other, with nothing left over to mark them as two.

It is the absence of any individuating content on either side that licenses reading them as one fact, not their bare coextension.

The formal vocabulary for this kind of identity is available in the contemporary grounding and essence literature. @schaffer2009 establishes grounding as a primitive ontological relation distinct from supervenience and reduction; @rosen2015 and @correiaSkiles2019 develop the formal tools for claims of the shape *x and y are the same fact described at different levels*.

The Modal Identity is one such claim. The possibility of change and the structural Conditions are not grounded in each other; grounding asymmetry would require the two entities that are not here. They are the same structural requirement under two descriptions. This is closer to what Correia and Skiles call generic identity than to standard grounding: one fact, two readings, no residue on either side.

One might still press that two distinct *modes of presentation* (the modal and the structural) could individuate two facts even where no extensional residue remains, as the morning star and the evening star present one object under graspably independent senses.

But the two readings here are not independently graspable. To grasp the modal reading (that change is possible) is already to grasp directed succession among distinct persisting states, which is the structural reading; and to grasp the structural reading is already to grasp the availability of transition, which is the modal one. There are not two senses that could be entertained singly, only one content approached from either side; the Fregean line to two facts requires two senses.

::: {.theorem}
**Modal Identity** · **T2** · *Theorem 2*

Nature read from the side of possibility: within the domain of full change-realizing structure, the possibility of change and the joint Conditions are one structural fact under two readings. □(◇C ↔ (T∧S∧Φ)), with the biconditional ranging over full Condition-instantiation rather than thin abstract analogues.[^2-6-6-modal-identity-scope]


:::

The Modal Identity licenses a further result developed at [§3.2](convergence.html#sec-3-2): if structure and change-possibility are one fact, then what are traditionally termed possible worlds are not alternative structures but alternative configurations within the one necessary structural ground. Modal plurality is combinatorial, not ontological.

*Necessity without collapse.* The Modal Identity establishes the necessity of the Conditions, not the necessity of any specific configuration within those Conditions. Structure is the stage on which Reality's history is enacted. The stage is necessary. No particular scene enacted on that stage is necessary. The contingency of specific configurations (which causal sequences occur, which relational positions are occupied, which particular substances interact) is fully preserved.

This distinction separates the argument from modal collapse: the mistaken inference that necessary structure entails necessary history. Modal collapse is the error of treating the necessity of the stage as entailing the necessity of the play. As established in [§2.3](the-argument.html#sec-2-3), □◇C is a claim about the modal status of a possibility, not a claim about the necessity of any actuality. What is necessarily true is that structure exists. What is contingent is everything enacted within it.

*Capacity and expression.* The same point can be put in the idiom of capacity. To assert □◇C is to say that Reality necessarily retains the *capacity* for change; to deny □C is to say that no particular *expression* of that capacity is necessary.

A capacity is real whether or not any given expression of it occurs, and it is the capacity, not its particular expressions, that the Necessity of Nature fixes. Which changes occur, in what order, on what occasion, is contingent expression; that there is a standing capacity to change at all is what is necessary. In this idiom, modal collapse is the error of reading the necessity of the capacity as the necessity of its expression, of mistaking the standing power for the particular act.

This capacity is not a power lying behind the structure and driving it. By the Modal Identity there is no such 'behind': Reality's capacity for change is not something T, S, and Φ *possess* but something they *are*, read from the side of possibility. To name the capacity is already to name the joint instantiation of the Conditions; the two are one structural fact under one description. The idiom of capacity adds no new ontology: it states the modal side of the identity in the language of power, what Reality *can* do, where the structural side states it in the language of constitution, what Reality *is*.

Necessity holds at the level of the Conditions. The physical descriptions are contingent expressions of those Conditions in this universe. Chapter 7 elaborates the confirmations, and the Modal Identity is what makes them confirmations rather than coincidences.[^2-6-6-modal-identity-ch4]

[^2-6-6-modal-identity-ch4]: T2 draws the necessity-without-collapse worry (modal collapse) engaged at [§4.4.9](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-4-9). Alternative structuralist readings of the identity claim come from Sider’s structuralism ([§4.4.7](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-4-7)) and structural realism ([§4.3.9](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-9)). The rival frozen-structure-as-mathematical-universe candidate the identity reading forecloses is pressed by Tegmark ([§4.3.7](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-7)) and the changeless-ground picture ([§4.2.1](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-2-1)).

The Modal Identity is the first of three readings of the Triconditional Identity ([§2.6.10](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-10)).

[^2-6-6-modal-identity-scope]: The necessitation in the Modal Identity is real / metaphysical: necessity in the modal structure, not closure of primary conceivability or epistemic openness. The two-dimensional question whether the biconditional remains primarily conceivable as false even where the secondary structural identity holds is engaged at [§4.1.2](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-2).

### 2.6.7 Triconditional Cross-Entailment {#sec-2-6-7}

This is the second of three readings of the Triconditional Identity ([§2.6.10](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-10)): Nature read from the cross-entailment among the three roles, the reading from which the Conditions point at one another. The first reading is the Modal Identity ([§2.6.6](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-6)); the third is the Ontological Identity ([§2.6.8](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-8)). The realizer move was worked three times at §[§2.6.2](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-2)–2.6.4, each pivoting on a different term, and gathered at [§2.6.5](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-5) as the *Mutual Containment Result*. Under this reading, the Conditions cross-entail within the realizer-level structure of genuine change: where one is fully instantiated as a Condition of change, the other two are co-instantiated. The claim is domain-restricted. It does not say that every abstract order is spatial and physical, every mathematical geometry temporal and causal, or every abstract bearer a change-process.

Pure mathematical abstraction is not a counterexample to the restricted theorem. A Kuratowski ordered pair, ⟨a, b⟩ := {{a}, {a, b}}, can instantiate abstract ordering and distinctness without temporal succession, spatial extension, or causal persistence. The theorem grants that point because a pure ordered pair is not a realizer of genuine change.

The deflationary move becomes relevant only when the ordered pair is offered as a complete account of an actual succession. Then an interpretation must identify its elements as states, their order as a before-and-after, and their connection as what makes the sequence one change rather than two unrelated entries. Those additional realizer conditions — not the set-theoretic pair by itself — bring the restricted T, S, and Φ domain into view.

Temporality requires causally structured succession among states, but causal structure requires a persistence medium (Φ) to carry influence from one state to the next, and relational extension (S) so that states can be genuinely distinct rather than differing only in their intrinsic properties. A causally structured succession with no persistence medium is a sequence of events connected by nothing. A causally structured succession whose states are distinguished only by their intrinsic properties (with no relational interval between them) provides no manifold across which causal influence can be transmitted.

Spatiality requires relational extension, but a relational structure requires temporal succession (T) for distinction between state-positions to be possible, and causal relata (Φ) for locations to be occupied and causally efficacious rather than empty geometrical abstractions. A relational structure with no temporal succession is a frozen geometry incapable of hosting movement. A relational structure with no causal relata is an unoccupied coordinate system with no capacity for differentiation or interaction.

Physicality requires a causal persistence medium, but causal persistence requires causally structured temporal succession (T) across which to persist and to transmit influence, and relational extension (S) to provide the relational structure across which that influence travels. A persistence medium with no temporal succession has nothing to persist through. A persistence medium with no relational extension collapses cause and effect into zero distance, eliminating the distinction between them.

Within any structure that realizes genuine change, the three Conditions form one realizer complex rather than three detachable ingredients. The cross-entailment is therefore not a theorem about arbitrary abstract structures. It is a theorem about full Condition-instantiation in the target domain: remove any role from a genuine change-realizer and the remaining two no longer realize change.

The three axes converge on one structural fact, and the cross-entailment can now be stated.

::: {.theorem}
**Triconditional Cross-Entailment** · **T3** · *Theorem 3*

Nature read from the cross-entailment among the three roles: within the realizer-level structure of genuine change, full instantiation of Temporality, Spatiality, or Physicality co-instantiates the other two. The roles are mutually implicating in that domain without being reducible to one another. T ↔ (S∧Φ), S ↔ (T∧Φ), Φ ↔ (T∧S), restricted to structures realizing genuine change.


:::

Consider any conversation. The example is offered as illustration of the load-bearing cross-entailment derivations above, not as a substitute for them; a reader who finds the conversation case unconvincing but accepts the formal derivations still has the result. Conversations are a usefully vivid instance because the joint requirement of all three Conditions shows up at the surface.

A conversation requires temporal direction: what was said before must shape what can be said next, and you cannot unsay what you have said. The earlier utterance is the ground of the later one in a way the later cannot reciprocate. Remove this and utterances float free of one another: nothing is a response to anything.

A conversation requires genuinely distinct positions in the exchange (speaker and listener, writer and reader), and the difference between them must be real rather than nominal. The positions need not always be occupied by two numerically distinct people: one person may answer an earlier thought or alternate roles across turns. What the exchange cannot lose is the distinction between address and uptake.

And a conversation requires persistence: the person who asked the question must be the person who receives the answer. The one who made the claim must be the one who can be held to it. Without persistence, there are no turns, because turns require someone to hand them to.

Remove any one of these Conditions and you do not have a simpler conversation. You are not having a conversation at all. Everything that makes exchange possible is already named in one sentence: between substances, across space, through time.

Within the target domain, to instantiate any one as a full Condition of genuine change is to instantiate all three. The qualification matters: an abstract order, geometry, or bearer considered outside a change-realizer is not a counterexample because it is not an instance of the theorem's restricted domain. What looks like three within a genuine change-realizer is one mutually implicating structure. The theorem establishes that restricted unity; it does not convert every abstract order, extension, or bearer into a change-realizer.

One consequence is worth stating on its own, since the argument of [§2.2.2](the-argument.html#sec-2-2-2) (Actuality Extends to the Ground) leans on it: the cross-entailment licenses not only that the three Conditions stand or fall together, but that anything in which even one of them is *actually present* thereby instantiates all three. That is what lets the actuality of structured experience reach its ground rather than stopping at experience.

::: {.corollary}
**Constitutive Instantiation** · **R8** · *Result of T3*

Where one of the Conditions (Temporality, Spatiality, or Physicality, or a determinate of one) is actually present in an experiencing, instantiated and not merely represented in content, all three are co-instantiated in that experiencing; and because the experiencing is a state its ground is in rather than a content the ground merely represents, the ground itself instantiates all three.


:::

The derivation from the cross-entailment to the ground runs in five steps:

::: {.argument}
**The Ground's Instantiation** · *The Line from the Cross-Entailment*

1. To instantiate a structural feature F is for F to be actually present; to encode F is to bear a representation of F while F itself is absent. A two-dimensional engine encodes three-dimensional space without occupying it: the distinction is what the result turns on.

1. *Cross-entailment (T3).* The actual instantiation of any one Condition-feature carries the conjunction of the other two with it.

1. An experience in which the Conditions are actually present is a state its ground is in, not a content it merely hosts and not a free-floating fact; the instantiation is therefore the ground's own rather than a structure the ground merely represents.

1. **Constitutive Instantiation.** So a ground of actually-structured experience instantiates T, S, and Φ. One that merely encoded them could underwrite a representation of such experience, but not an experience in which the structure is actually present, and it is the latter that [§2.2.2](the-argument.html#sec-2-2-2) requires.

1. Whether weak or strong, emergence may relocate where a feature is first instantiated; it cannot convert actual instantiation into mere encoding. Once the feature is actually present, step 2 fires.

:::

*The encoding dilemma.* The result reaches the ground even without treating the experience as the ground's own state. Take any candidate ground of an actually structured experience. Either it instantiates the experienced Conditions outright (and since experience exhibits all three, so does it) or it merely *encodes* them.

But an encoding that grounds a live experience is not ontologically free: a representation borne and read as that ground is a tokened activity, carried in a medium (Φ), across distinct vehicle-elements (S), processed across steps (T). So the encoding horn instantiates the Conditions no less than the instantiation horn, and the deflationist's ‘it is only represented’ is self-defeating.

The dilemma needs neither a grounding-priority premise (the level-invariance line, [§2.2.2](the-argument.html#sec-2-2-2)) nor the cross-entailment: experience already presents all three, and each horn carries all three to the ground.

Its one limit is the temporal step: a frozen, never-read encoding need not succeed in time. The line is therefore restricted to grounds of *actual, ongoing* experience, where the encoding is being processed. An untokened, purely abstract encoding grounds no live experience, as the Kuratowski reply above already shows.

To picture the two horns concretely: a game engine renders a three-dimensional scene on a flat panel. It *encodes* depth — objects occlude one another, distances scale with position — without instantiating it: nothing in the pixels stands behind anything else, and the third dimension the scene represents is simply absent.

That is the first horn, encoding without instantiation. But the rendering is also a live process: it runs frame after frame (T), across distinct cells and pixels laid out on the panel (S), in a substrate that persists through the computation (Φ).

The feature it encodes can be missing; the Conditions that carry the encoding cannot.

You can encode a structure you do not instantiate, but you cannot run the encoding without instantiating Temporality, Spatiality, and Physicality — which is the second horn, and why the deflationist's 'it is only represented' still arrives at the ground.

At the level of logic, the same fact: temporal logic, spatial logic, and substantial logic are not three logics in coordination but one logic read along three axes: the metalogical architecture is developed at [§2.10](the-argument.html#sec-2-10).

The cross-entailment the Triconditional Cross-Entailment names structurally is shared logical form. To be one of T, S, Φ is already to share the logical aspect the other two are: what reads as succession from one axis, as distinction from another, as carrying-through from the third, *is* the same logic showing its three faces.

*What is identified.* A consequence follows that governs the rest of the argument. A coordinate does not have an essence that it then expresses. It essentially expresses. What the coordinate does viewed as static property is its essence; what the coordinate does viewed as activity is its expression: the same structural fact from two directions. Neither direction reaches something the other misses.

Essence without expression is a coordinate without axes: the phrase retains its grammar but has lost its referent. The bridge to the essence / expression collapse runs through the realizer move of [§2.6.1](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-1): what makes a structural feature a structural feature, rather than a labeled placeholder, is its operativity within the structure it figures in.

A coordinate that has no axes to figure in is a label, not a coordinate; an essence that has no expression to be the essence *of* is a name, not an essence.

At the structural level the operativity is constitutive of the feature: the essence does not stand behind the expression as a further determinable, because the expression *is* what the essence consists in. There is no hidden what-it-is behind the expressing, because the expressing is the what-it-is.

This is what makes the severances of Chapter 6 total rather than partial: negating what the Conditions do is not stripping away an outer layer to reveal a residual essence beneath. It is negating the essence itself.[^2-6-7-cross-entailment-ch4]

[^2-6-7-cross-entailment-ch4]: The cross-entailment among the three roles (T3) is engaged in Chapter 4. The Humean denial of necessary connection between distinct existences presses directly at the cross-entailment site ([§4.1.4](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-4)), conventionalism about laws at [§4.1.7](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-7), Quine's denial of the analytic–essential distinction the cross-entailment relies on at [§4.1.6](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-6), and Sider's structuralism on lawlike structure at [§4.4.7](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-4-7).

### 2.6.8 Ontological Identity {#sec-2-6-8}

The being-side of the three Conditions is the third reading of the Triconditional Identity ([§2.6.10](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-10)). T, S, and Φ were established at [§2.4.2](the-argument.html#sec-2-4-2) as constitutive of any being whatsoever: no gap opens at the structural level between how a being presents and what it consists in, because the Conditions are not surface features with a hidden essence but the being's essence itself. The facthood line at [§2.4.4](the-argument.html#sec-2-4-4) reaches the same constitutive conclusion from the side of what any state of affairs requires. Where the Modal Identity named structure as possibility ([§2.6.6](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-6)) and the Triconditional Cross-Entailment named it from cross-entailment among the three roles ([§2.6.7](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-7)), the *Ontological Identity* names it from the side of being: the reading at which T∧S∧Φ shows up as what being consists in. Same shape, different side. These are three logical-categorical readings of the same Nature: modal (necessity), nomological (law), ontological (being).

A being is not a substrate on which T, S, and Φ are imposed from outside. A being is something that persists (Φ), distinct from other things (S), across transition (T). A Φ that does not persist across any S or T is no being. An S that does not separate any Φs across any T is not a space. A T that does not host any Φ succeeding across any S is not a time. The three Conditions are not a set of requirements beings meet. The three Conditions *are* what *being* *consists in*.

This yields the Ontological Identity.

::: {.theorem}
**Ontological Identity** · **T4** · *Theorem 4*

Nature read from the side of being: to be in Nature is to instantiate T∧S∧Φ. Not to match T, S, and Φ as a necessary condition; to be T, S, and Φ in operation as a being. What has being in Nature is T, S, and Φ in operation; what T, S, and Φ are in operation, has being. No residue on either side.


:::

Ontic Structural Realism provides the contemporary philosophical ally. @ladymanRoss2007 argue that fundamental physics describes relational and structural features rather than intrinsic natures: that the ontology physics delivers is structure, not substance-in-the-classical-sense. @french2014 develops the same position for quantum mechanics.

The Ontological Identity is not Ontic Structural Realism, but it is continuous with it: where Ontic Structural Realism is an interpretive thesis about what physics describes, the Ontological Identity is a modal thesis about what any being must be. The structural realist, asked what the structure consists in, answers with the relational fabric physics specifies; the present account answers with T, S, and Φ as the minimal structural conditions any being must instantiate. The two positions converge on the same fact from opposite directions: physics ends up with structure because structure is what there was to be.

A theist, idealist, or dual-aspect realist can keep their vocabulary, but whatever they propose as a being in their account already instantiates T∧S∧Φ, and instantiating T∧S∧Φ *is* what being in Nature *means* here. The being-question is not a substrate choice to be disputed. It is the structural shape of any being at all. The Modal Identity, the Triconditional Cross-Entailment, and the Ontological Identity converge at the *Triconditional Identity* in [§2.6.10](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-10): three readings, one Nature, under three logical lenses; the thesis is drawn at [§2.8.3](the-argument.html#sec-2-8-3).[^2-6-8-ontological-identity-ch4]

[^2-6-8-ontological-identity-ch4]: The being-side reading of T4 (that T∧S∧Φ is what being in Nature consists in) is engaged in Chapter 4. Idealism makes being a mode of mind rather than structure ([§4.3.5](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-5)), Russellian monism posits intrinsic categorical natures behind the structure ([§4.3.3](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-3)), bundle theory and tropes read being as bundle rather than Φ-in-operation ([§4.3.10](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-10)), and mereological nihilism denies the composites the being-reading addresses ([§4.3.11](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-11)); structural realism is the closest ally that nonetheless diverges on what the structure consists in ([§4.3.9](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-9)). The classical-theist reply (that God is being itself, held exempt from instantiating T∧S∧Φ rather than counted as a being that instantiates it) is taken up under divine simplicity, on which God is identical with subsistent existence rather than a being that has it ([§5.2.1](rival-ultimates.html#sec-5-2-1)), Neoplatonism and the One held to be beyond being ([§5.3.2](rival-ultimates.html#sec-5-3-2)), and the via negativa, which withholds positive structural predication of God ([§5.2.2](rival-ultimates.html#sec-5-2-2)).

### 2.6.9 Triunity of Nature {#sec-2-6-9}

Three readings have been named: the Modal Identity ([§2.6.6](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-6)), the Triconditional Cross-Entailment ([§2.6.7](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-7)), and the Ontological Identity ([§2.6.8](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-8)). Do they pick out three facts, or one?

The Triconditions are the same in each. The T that appears in the Modal Identity (◇C ↔ T∧S∧Φ) is the same T that appears in the Triconditional Cross-Entailment and the same T the Ontological Identity names as the being-condition of any real thing. No equivocation runs across the three uses: each letter names the same Condition, and the co-extension established across §[§2.6](the-argument.html#sec-2-6) is the co-extension of these Conditions, not of three different trios of Conditions that happen to share notation.

What the three differ in is not the Triconditions but the layer. The Ontological Identity takes the Triconditions at the physical layer: T, S, and Φ *are* what any being *consists in*, what any physical thing is, across distance, through time. The Triconditional Cross-Entailment takes it at the law-of-physics layer: any regularity is a regularity in what persists (Φ), across distinction (S), through succession (T): the Triconditions in lawful operation. The Modal Identity takes it at the logical layer: what can be the case is what can host T, S, and Φ together: the Triconditions in modal form. Three layers, the same Triconditions.

The reduction runs from the physical layer up. A physical thing is a being acting across distance through time: it is Φ distinguished in S and succeeding in T. That is not a description of a physical thing; it *is* what being a physical thing *consists in*. There is no residue after the Triconditions specify the being: no further constituent that makes the being physical in some way the Triconditions did not capture. The Ontological Identity is the claim that being physical and instantiating T∧S∧Φ *are* the same fact, not two facts that match.[^2-6-9-thin-loaded-descent-ch4]

The next reduction follows at the level of lawful structure. A physical law constrains what physical things do; on a regularity account, it is described through patterns in that activity, while governing and primitivist accounts deny that laws reduce to regularities. Either way, its instances involve distinguishable states (S) of beings or realizers (Φ) across transitions or dependency-order (T). Physics is not a substrate beside the physical: the nomological reading describes the lawful organization of the same structural field the ontological reading describes from the side of being. The Triconditional Cross-Entailment is the Ontological Identity read through law, not a commitment to a regularity theory of laws.

The final reduction closes at the logical layer. ◇C ↔ T∧S∧Φ does not add possibility to the Triconditions as a further property. It names what possibility is: the co-instantiation of the Triconditions. But the co-instantiation is what the Ontological Identity names as the activity of being and what the Triconditional Cross-Entailment names as lawful regularity. Possibility is not a third domain. It is the Triconditions' modal description: what must hold for the Triconditions to hold anywhere. The Modal Identity is the Ontological Identity described as possibility.

*What is identified.* The three readings are one Nature read under three lenses: the *Triunity of Nature*. The readings converge because each names the same inseparability of T, S, and Φ from a different side: Modal from possibility, Nomological from cross-entailment among the roles, Ontological from being-instantiation. The modal, the nomological, and the ontological are not three layers connected isomorphically. Possibility, laws, and being are not three layers: they are one fact described modally, nomologically, and ontologically. What moves between the three is identity under description, not structural analogy. The compression here does not mean empirical physics reduces to formal logic; it means the lawful structure physics describes and the modal structure logic names are the same Triconditions under different descriptions. Each layer resolves into the same logical form. This identity is established here for Reality as the change-hosting structural complex: the Triconditions read under three lenses. Whether any candidate necessary ground could stand outside it (in particular one specified as standing outside change, the classical theist's atemporal ground, granted only the thin Conditions at [§2.6.3](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-3)) is not assumed here but settled at [§2.8.6](the-argument.html#sec-2-8-6). There, Exclusivity of Nature (Theorem 7) shows any such ground either instantiates the Triconditions in the loaded sense or is a variant of ∅.

A modal-collapse worry has to be flagged and disarmed. The Triunity says the three readings are one fact under three lenses, but possibility and being are typically taken as distinct categories (some things are possible without being actual, and *being possible* is not the same property as *being actual*). The Triunity does not collapse this distinction at the level of individual propositions. It compresses at the level of the structural Triconditions: what makes ◇C true, what any actual being is, and what any lawful regularity describes is the same Triconditions (T, S, Φ) under three logical-categorical readings. These are three readings of the Triconditions, not three properties of one proposition. The distinction between *being possible* and *being actual* survives at the propositional level; the compression operates between *what makes possibility possible* and *what makes actuality actual*: at that structural level, the answer is the same Triconditions, read under modal, nomological, and ontological lenses.

That shared structure is logical form. These three are logical-categorical readings of one Nature, drawn from the three primary lenses analytic metaphysics has developed: necessity, law, being. The three logics of the Conditions (succession, distinction, carrying-through) and the three logics of the readings (necessity, law, being) are two independent axes of the same logical form. Both axes are closed by logical considerations rather than by stipulation: no fourth Condition can be added because the three already enumerate what change requires (the Condition-Individuation of [§2.6.11](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-11)), and no fourth reading can be added because the three already enumerate the logical-categorical readings under which Nature is read. The Conditions and the readings *are* one logic read along two independent axes. Logic is not a fourth result alongside the Modal Identity, the Triconditional Cross-Entailment, and the Ontological Identity. It is the perspective from which the three are readings, and the shape the three share: what makes their convergence intelligible at all.

The reduction runs one level deeper. If the three are three descriptions of one fact, the descriptions cannot come apart at the register line. Any description in any register already deploys the vocabulary of every register, because the fact it describes *is* the fact every register describes.

A physical description *is* already a nomological description *is* already a modal description: not by translation, but because the registers are angles on one thing. Point at a stone in the physical register and you are pointing at what persists through time (Φ), stands across distance (S), and holds in succession (T). The same pointing, in the modal register, points at what can be the case. No phenomenal description, unpacked, turns out not already analytical. No analytical description, grounded, turns out not already phenomenal.

@sellars1956 called the separable given a myth. @mcdowell1994 pressed the conceptual all the way into experience. The inseparability they noticed at the epistemic level is what the cross-entailments force at the structural level. The registers are not sides of description that might come apart. They *are* one act of describing one fact.[^2-6-9-triunity-ch4]

What that one fact is, named, is delivered at [§2.6.10](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-10).

[^2-6-9-triunity-ch4]: The Triunity claim (that the modal, nomological, and ontological readings are one Nature rather than three independent layers) is engaged in Chapter 4. Modal collapse is the worry the Triunity must disarm at the propositional level ([§4.4.9](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-4-9)), Lewis reads modal realism as a three-layer picture ([§4.4.1](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-4-1)), Sider's structuralism ([§4.4.7](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-4-7)) and structural realism press on what the convergence consists in ([§4.3.9](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-9)), and Quine's anti-distinction pressure targets the layer-as-reading move ([§4.1.6](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-6)).

[^2-6-9-thin-loaded-descent-ch4]: Whether the thin Conditions granted to an atemporal ground (mere priority, distinctness, and dependence) descend to the loaded reading (directional succession and causal carrying), the classical-theist and Neoplatonic line, is established at [§2.8.6](the-argument.html#sec-2-8-6) in two stages. Its modal core is discharged in-chapter at [§2.8.6](the-argument.html#sec-2-8-6) (Exclusivity of Nature, Theorem 7): any candidate necessary ground either instantiates T, S, and Φ in the loaded sense (structure under another description) or forecloses rather than enables any possible state of affairs, a variant of ∅, on owned Chapter-2 machinery (the Triconditional Cross-Entailment [§2.6.7](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-7) and the Incoherence of ∅ [§2.7.2](the-argument.html#sec-2-7-2)). The strongest named formulations are then tested at [§5.2.1](rival-ultimates.html#sec-5-2-1) (Divine Simplicity), [§5.3.2](rival-ultimates.html#sec-5-3-2) (Neoplatonism), and [§5.2.2](rival-ultimates.html#sec-5-2-2) (The Via Negativa).

### 2.6.10 Triconditional Identity {#sec-2-6-10}

The three results from §[§2.6.6](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-6)–2.6.8, together with the Triunity of Nature ([§2.6.9](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-9)), are not separate discoveries assembled here. They are three ways of reading one Nature at the resolution the chapter has established: the necessary co-instantiation of Temporality, Spatiality, and Physicality as the full change-realizing structural complex. They do not turn every abstract order, geometry, or bearer into an instance of that complex. Nature is triconditional: jointly characterized by three readings whose unity *is* what Nature is.

The inheritance chain runs explicitly: the Modal Identity (□(◇C ↔ T∧S∧Φ)) is supplied at [§2.6.6](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-6); the Triconditional Cross-Entailment (cross-axis cross-entailment T↔(S∧Φ), S↔(T∧Φ), Φ↔(T∧S)) at [§2.6.7](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-7); the Ontological Identity (the structural shape of any being) at [§2.6.8](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-8); the Triunity (the three readings are one Nature read under three lenses) at [§2.6.9](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-9).

That one Nature, named under its joint characterization, *is* the Triconditional Identity. The Triconditional Identity is not a fourth result built on top of the three readings. It is the derivation that the three were one Nature all along: Nature characterized by three readings whose unity is the name. Each reading establishes a fact of nature; the three are jointly the constitutive facts the Triconditional Identity comprises through its three Conditions.

::: {.theorem}
**Triconditional Identity** · **T5** · *Theorem 5*

Nature is triconditional: jointly characterized by the Modal Identity, the Triconditional Cross-Entailment, and the Ontological Identity, whose unity is what Nature is. Nature is the necessary full change-realizing complex of T, S, and Φ. The direct derivational result is the definitional identity N ↔ (T∧S∧Φ): Nature just is the joint structural complex, box-free. Necessity is a further, separately earned result — [§2.8.5](the-argument.html#sec-2-8-5) predicates necessity of N as Theorem 6 — and only with that necessity in hand do the boxed biconditionals follow, read as generic identity only on the no-surplus argument at the full Condition resolution: N ↔ □(T∧S∧Φ), N ↔ □◇C, □(T∧S∧Φ) ↔ □◇C.


:::

These biconditionals do not all earn identity the same way, and one does not earn it by definition at all. *Nature* was introduced at [§1.4.4](groundwork.html#sec-1-4-4) and fixed again at the opening of Chapter 2 as the joint structural complex T∧S∧Φ; [§2.8.5](the-argument.html#sec-2-8-5) states its necessity as Theorem 6. The clause relating Nature to that complex is therefore a strict *definitional* identity: its right-hand side *is* the definiendum of *Nature*, not a predicate that merely happens to be co-extensive with it across all worlds. The clauses relating either Nature or the complex to □◇C are not definitional identities; what is proved of them directly is the necessary biconditional. They are read as identities on the separate ground argued at [§2.6.6](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-6), that between the Conditions and the possibility of change there is no individuating surplus on either side, which makes them one structural fact rather than two necessarily-linked ones. That further reading is a *generic* identity, not a definitional one; a reader who grants only the biconditional still has the necessity result and forgoes only the ontological gloss [§2.6.6](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-6) builds on it. The notation marks logical equivalence throughout; the definitional identity is earned outright, while the generic identity is the stronger reading the biconditional will bear.

Read from inside Nature, N ↔ □◇C names *Modal Pressure* directly: the necessary possibility of change propagates through the modal-structural link because Nature is necessary. Nature is not a substrate that houses a further pressure; Nature *is* the necessary co-instantiation of T, S, and Φ, and on the generic-identity reading argued at [§2.6.6](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-6) that co-instantiation and the necessary possibility of change are one structural fact under two descriptions, not two facts that merely track each other. When this work calls Nature necessary, what is strictly proved necessary is the Triconditions' co-instantiation; a reader who takes only the biconditional keeps that result, while a reader who grants the generic identity reads it as the very fact □◇C names. Point at Nature and, on that reading, you are pointing at what □◇C names.

This is the formal spine of the *Necessity of Nature*. Not the empirical claim that the physical world happens to exist. Not the metaphysical claim that the physical is the only substrate. The modal result that the modal, the nomological, and the ontological are three readings of one Nature (three logical-categorical readings under the three primary lenses analytic metaphysics has developed) and that the Triconditions, necessarily instantiated, *are* the Triconditional Identity. The thesis is named at [§2.8.3](the-argument.html#sec-2-8-3) and fixed formally at [§2.8.5](the-argument.html#sec-2-8-5).

Three readings, one Nature: three logical-categorical readings under three lenses. The Modal Identity reads T∧S∧Φ from the side of possibility: the Conditions whose joint instantiation is co-extensive with ◇C across all worlds. The Triconditional Cross-Entailment reads them from their cross-entailment: each conjoined with the other two along three axes. The Ontological Identity reads them from the side of bearing: the structural shape of any being at all. The Conditions are three; the readings are three; and the readings cross the Conditions perpendicularly, not three parallel trios, but a 3×3 grid: each Condition shown under three readings, each reading carrying all three Conditions. The 3×3 grid is logic mapping onto Conditions and readings together: both axes are exhaustively closed by logical considerations, not by stipulation. The reading is plural; what is read is single: the Triconditional Identity.

The three are readings of one Nature: the one Nature whose readings they are. The Triconditional Identity is the name.[^2-6-10-triconditional-identity-ch4]

[^2-6-10-triconditional-identity-ch4]: Theorem 5 (the joint claim that Nature is the necessary co-instantiation of T∧S∧Φ and that this is identical to □◇C) is engaged in Chapter 4: modal collapse ([§4.4.9](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-4-9)), Williamson's necessitism ([§4.4.6](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-4-6)), Sider's structuralism ([§4.4.7](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-4-7)), modal fictionalism ([§4.4.4](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-4-4)), Tegmark's mathematical universe ([§4.3.7](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-7)), eliminativism and illusionism ([§4.3.2](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-2)), structural realism ([§4.3.9](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-9)), and the question whether possibility has a source ([§4.1.10](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-10)).

### 2.6.11 No Fourth Condition {#sec-2-6-11}

The Triconditional Identity ([§2.6.10](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-10), Theorem 5) names Nature as jointly characterized by exactly three Conditions: Temporality, Spatiality, and Physicality. Why three, and why these three? ∅ is dissolved on the side of being at [§2.7](the-argument.html#sec-2-7), showing that no Reality coherently lacks any of T, S, or Φ; the three are derived from what change's possibility requires at [§2.4](the-argument.html#sec-2-4); the cross-entailments that show the three are one Nature are worked at §[§2.6.1](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-1)–2.6.10. Each of these results works from within the framework's own derivational machinery. A *Condition-Individuation Criterion* supplies an external, methodological check: it screens what counts as a candidate Condition in the first place, before the derivational work runs.

::: {.lemma}
**Condition-Individuation** · **L4** · *Lemma toward Triconditional Identity*

X is a Condition of Reality only if X comes with a natural quantifier-pair ⟨*X-positive, X-negative*⟩ such that the Law of Excluded Middle applies exhaustively to existence-claims along the X-axis (every existence-claim at X-instantiation is determinately either X-positive or X-negative, with no third option) and X is irreducible to any other LEM-applicable axis.


:::

A Condition is a real existence-axis along which any question of being has a determinate yes-or-no answer, and the axis is not merely another existence-axis under a different description.

The three Conditions satisfy the Criterion via three quantifier-pairs that ordinary language has independently carved out. Physicality (Φ) takes the pair *something / no thing*: some thing has being, or no thing does, and the binary is exhaustive. Spatiality (S) takes the pair *somewhere / nowhere*: some thing is at some location, or no thing is anywhere, and the binary is exhaustive. Temporality (T) takes the pair *sometime / never*: some thing happens at some time, or nothing ever happens, and the binary is exhaustive. That ordinary language has *exactly* these three quantifier-pairs for existence-instantiation, and no fourth of equal grammatical naturalness, is weak structural evidence: confirmation rather than derivation. The Criterion's load-bearing work runs through the LEM-clause and the irreducibility-clause; the grammar observation is an independent indicator that Nature's three existence-axes are tracked by ordinary language as well as by structural derivation. The load-bearing claim does not rest on the grammar observation.

*The two-part screen.* The Criterion has two clauses, both necessary. The LEM-clause screens for axes along which existence-instantiation is bivalent; the irreducibility-clause screens for axes not already reducible to other axes screened-in. A candidate that passes the LEM-clause may still fail the irreducibility-clause if Theorem 5's biconditional N ↔ □(T∧S∧Φ) ↔ □◇C shows the candidate to be co-equivalent with one already among the Triconditions. Together the two clauses give a tight individuation procedure: produce the quantifier-pair, demonstrate LEM-at-existence, demonstrate irreducibility. Earn all three and the candidate has Condition-status. Fail any one and it does not.

*Candidate fourth Conditions, screened.* The Criterion rules out otherwise tempting additions. *Cause* as a fourth Condition fails on metaphysical grounds: causation is a relation among Φ-instances across T-succession and S-extension, not an axis along which existence is itself instantiated. To be caused is to be a Φ-being whose persistence is conditioned by other Φ-beings' prior persistence (T-direction) across some interval (S-relation); causation is a derived structure within the three existing axes, not a fourth. Grammar confirms this: no natural quantifier-pair *somehow / nohow* of equal standing has emerged, and *every event has a cause or no event does* is not LEM-at-existence but a contingency-relation claim, handled in [§2.8.4](the-argument.html#sec-2-8-4) *Necessity Precedes Contingency*. Hume's worry about necessary causal connection [-@hume1739; -@hume1748] is the canonical opponent in this territory. *Information* as a fourth Condition fails by similar lights: information-instantiation reduces to Φ-instantiation under a particular description and does not carve a new existence-axis. *Consciousness* as a fourth Condition fails because experiences are had by Φ-beings at S-positions in T-succession; experiences are a particular kind of Φ-instantiation rather than a fourth existence-axis (Chapter 7). *Change* passes the LEM-clause via the modal-axis pairing *possible / impossible* (◇C / ¬◇C), but fails the irreducibility-clause: Theorem 5's N ↔ □◇C identifies □◇C with □(T∧S∧Φ), so the modal-axis is co-equivalent with the three existence-axes rather than a fourth independent axis. ◇C is the modal-side of the same Nature, not a fourth Condition.

*From screen to closure.* Taken by itself, the Criterion's force is asymmetric: it places the burden of proof on any proposed fourth (produce the quantifier-pair, demonstrate LEM-at-existence on it, demonstrate irreducibility to the Triconditions). Without all three, the proposal has not earned Condition-status. Set beside the Sufficiency of Structure result ([§2.4.10](the-argument.html#sec-2-4-10)), the screen adds a further constraint. If a candidate fourth X is necessary for the possibility of change, then ◇C → X; the converse at [§2.4.10](the-argument.html#sec-2-4-10) gives T∧S∧Φ → ◇C; chaining them yields T∧S∧Φ → X. Thus any candidate fourth must obtain wherever the Triconditions are instantiated. That entailment does not by itself prove reducibility: an entailed property may still be irreducible. The remaining work is therefore exactly the Criterion's second clause. A genuine fourth must show that it is not merely a consequence, determinable, relation, or redescription of the three despite being entailed by them. The argument closes the easy routes to a fourth and leaves a precise irreducibility burden rather than pretending that entailment alone settles identity.[^2-6-11-condition-individuation-ch4]

What the foreclosure does not settle lies one level back, and the limit is worth marking exactly. The result runs *through* the analysis of change as causally structured succession among distinct, persisting states ([§1.3](groundwork.html#sec-1-3); the framework-invariant form at [§2.4.5](the-argument.html#sec-2-4-5)): succession, distinction, and exchange. That a fourth is foreclosed *given* that analysis is now proven; that the three-role analysis is itself the privileged carving of Reality is not established from outside it. The analysis is defended by the necessity of each role and by the self-application that any rival analysis is itself a change exhibiting the three: both showing the Triconditions cannot be thought past, not that a carving beyond all analysis has been inspected. The residual question is therefore not whether a fourth Condition might be articulated within the framework (it cannot be) but whether one is bound to the starting analysis of change at all, the form deflationism presses at [§4.1.8](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-8).

*Literature.* The Criterion redirects three lines of work. Aristotle on LEM (*De Interpretatione* 9; *Metaphysics* Γ 3–4) is the historical ancestor for treating LEM as ontologically rather than merely logically binding. Quine [-@quine1948] and the broader Quinean tradition treat existence as univocal (the value of a bound variable). The Criterion does not need to reject that thesis: one univocal existential quantifier can range over beings that necessarily satisfy several irreducible structural conditions. Its disagreement with Quine is instead about whether T, S, and Φ mark objective joints that every existent must instantiate, not about whether *exists* changes meaning from one axis to another. Sider [-@sider2011] and the structural-realism literature treat Reality as jointly carved at specific structural joints; the Criterion is a specific structural-realist commitment about which joints Reality has. Intuitionist reservations about LEM (Brouwer, Heyting) apply to unbounded mathematical claims; dialetheist reservations (Priest) apply to paradoxical propositions; neither bears on the Criterion's restriction to empirical existence-claims along the three Conditions.

[^2-6-11-condition-individuation-ch4]: Condition-Individuation (the two-clause LEM-plus-irreducibility screen on candidate Conditions) is engaged in Chapter 4. The canonical opponent of the LEM-applicable axis carving is Quine's existence-univocity ([§4.1.6](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-6)); structural realism and Sider are the closest ally that nonetheless diverges on which joints ([§4.3.9](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-9)), Tegmark's mathematical universe presses for fourth-Condition mathematical axes ([§4.3.7](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-7)), and conventionalism/anti-realism about laws presses on the irreducibility-clause ([§4.1.7](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-7)).

### 2.6.12 Necessity's Nature {#sec-2-6-12}

The Triconditional Identity ([§2.6.10](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-10), Theorem 5) stated the identity N ↔ □(T∧S∧Φ) ↔ □◇C. Condition-Individuation ([§2.6.11](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-11)) supplied the methodological screen that licenses the count of three. The same identity reads from the side of language: what Theorem 5 means for the genitive *the nature of X*: for X = necessity in the limit case, and for X more widely.

::: {.argument}
**Conditioned-Nature** · *The Derivation*

1. Theorem 5 ([§2.6.10](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-10)) identified the modal constraint with the Conditions: N ↔ □(T∧S∧Φ). The relata of any genitive *the nature of X* are thereby fixed: there is nothing for a nature to be other than what the constraint constrains.

1. Take the limit case, X = necessity. *The Necessity of Nature* (Theorem 6, [§2.8.5](the-argument.html#sec-2-8-5)) reads as predication: Nature is necessary. *The nature of necessity* (this section) reads as identification: what necessity is, is Nature. Both genitives issue from □(T∧S∧Φ) and refer to the same N; the apparent chiasmus collapses because Theorem 5 has identified the relata.

1. The collapse does not depend on necessity being the limit case. Anything that has a nature has it by standing in some determinate relation to T, S, and Φ: instantiating them, articulating one of their structural features, or being abstracted from them.

1. There is no fourth dimension along which the *of* in *the nature of* could refer. A candidate relatum bearing no relation whatever to T, S, and Φ is not a nature but nothing, in the sense developed at [§2.7](the-argument.html#sec-2-7).

1. Therefore, for any X that articulates a structural feature of N, the nature of X terminates in that feature: the X-describable feature of N.

:::

The argument closes on a single result.

::: {.lemma}
**Conditioned-Nature** · **L5** · *Lemma toward Wigner Dissolution, Essence-Description*

For any X that articulates a structural feature of N, the nature of X = the X-describable feature of N.


:::

Conditioned-Nature reads the genitive *"nature of"* as a fixed-point identity restricted to a structural region. Necessity is the limit case in which the region is the whole of N: its nature is N entire. Mathematics is the case in which the region is the quantifiability of N: its nature is the structure mathematics describes, and that structure is just the quantifiable face of T, S, and Φ. Conditioned-Nature's force is that nothing in the schema requires a second realm of natures floating free of the Conditions. Each *nature of X* terminates in a structural feature of N.

*Cases.* Logic articulates determinate-distinguishability: a structural feature carried jointly by T (succession in inference), S (relation among premises and conclusion), and Φ (the stability of distinguishables across the inference); the nature of logic is the determinately-distinguishable structure of N. Geometry articulates extension and figure: S directly. Temporal ordering enters when geometrical reasoning is performed or geometrical structure is physically realized, not as part of abstract geometry's content merely by definition. On the present account, the nature of geometry is the extension-aspect of N. Propositional content articulates truth-aptness, which presupposes T, S, and Φ for there to be anything for a proposition to be true of; the nature of propositional content is the structure of N as susceptible to true description.

In each case the standard objection (*but these are abstracta, not features of Nature*) concedes the point in different language. Abstracta are abstractions *of* something; Conditioned-Nature names what they are abstractions of. The strongest Platonist [@godel1947; @maddy1990] holds mathematical objects to be irreducibly abstract entities, existing independently of T, S, and Φ. Conditioned-Nature's reply, at its strongest: a mathematical object that bears *no* relation whatever to T, S, and Φ would be undetectable, inapplicable, and unstatable: there would be no way to refer to it, pick it out, or do anything with it. The mathematical objects Platonists are willing to defend are exactly those that bear *some* relation to T, S, and Φ: typically the relation of being *describable* in a language hosted by T-S-Φ-bearing speakers, or the relation of being *applicable* to T-S-Φ-bearing systems. Conditioned-Nature names that relation as the constitutive relation through which mathematical objects have a nature at all. Platonism about mathematical existence is compatible with Conditioned-Nature; Platonism about a nature wholly outside the Conditions is not.

::: {.corollary}
**Wigner Dissolution** · **R9** · *Result of L5*

Mathematics and Nature are not two domains whose alignment requires explanation. Mathematics articulates the quantifiable aspect of Nature; its applicability to Nature is constitutive, not contingent. The puzzle of mathematics' unreasonable effectiveness in the natural sciences [@wigner1960] dissolves at the level of presupposition.


:::

Conditioned-Nature denies the presupposition that mathematics and Nature occupy distinct realms whose correspondence requires a further story. The quantifiable aspect of Nature is what mathematics articulates, and the articulation is identical with what is articulated. There are not two things to align. The dissolution does not predict which specific mathematical structures will be effective in which physical domains: that remains an empirical question, settled by the working of physics rather than by the Lemma. What dissolves is the framing of Wigner's question: applicability is not a cosmic coincidence requiring metaphysical explanation, because mathematics articulates the structural conditions that constitute Nature and the empirical work of physics is the work of finding the right articulation for a given domain. *That* mathematics is effective dissolves; *which* mathematical structures are effective for what remains substantively physical.

::: {.corollary}
**Essence-Description** · **R10** · *Result of L5*
