By the Triconditional Cross-Entailment ([§2.6.7](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-7)), instantiation of any one Condition analytically requires instantiation of the conjunction of the other two. Therefore any G that instantiates exactly one or two Conditions is internally incoherent: G's instantiation of (say) T entails T∧S∧Φ by [§2.6.7](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-7), contradicting the supposition that G instantiates exactly one or two. There is no consistent specification of a partial-overlap G. The remaining options are full overlap (G instantiates all three, hence G is structure under another name) and zero overlap (G instantiates none, hence G is ∅). The trichotomy is logically exhaustive.

The three moves close the space together, and the exclusivity of structure can now be stated.

::: {.theorem}
**Exclusivity of Nature** · **T7** · *Theorem 7*

The necessary ground of any possible state of affairs is uniquely structure: T, S, and Φ together. Any proposed alternative is either (i) functionally equivalent to T, S, and Φ (in which case it is structure under another description), or (ii) genuinely incommensurable with T, S, and Φ (in which case it forecloses rather than enables any possible state of affairs and is a variant of ∅). There is no coherent third option. Nature is not one necessary being among possible others. Within the present modal constraint, necessity has no content outside it; whether a necessary being might stand outside the natural order is engaged in Chapters 5 and 6, not foreclosed here.


:::

These three Conditions jointly constitute Nature: Reality’s necessary structural constitution, not one structure among possible alternatives. There is no further structure for them to be an instance of.

Every structural fact (however abstractly described) is a fact about how T, S, and Φ are instantiated. The structuralist intuition in philosophy of mathematics, that mathematical objects are structures rather than entities, survives the result. What does not survive is the further claim that those structures inhabit a Platonic realm distinct from Nature.

The result strengthens the case at its weakest joint. Earlier physicalism over-credited Φ relative to T and S, treating matter-energy as the basement on which the dimensions rest, when in fact Φ presupposes the dimensions to obtain at all ([§2.8.3](the-argument.html#sec-2-8-3)). The Necessity of Nature instead treats T, S, and Φ as co-equal structural roles and derives its content from modal necessity, so the thesis stops being contingent on what fundamental physics will eventually say and becomes a modal claim that holds regardless. The modal step also delivers what a contingent, initial-state account cannot: structural closure of the why-anything-at-all question (dissolved by the Incoherence of ∅, not deferred to physics) and structural resolution of the why-stop question for the necessity machinery (answered by what structural incapacity consists in, not by stipulation). The necessary-being pressure is foreclosed structurally rather than left open or redirected to physics. The full comparative-theory evaluation is engaged in Chapter 4 ([§4.3](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3), [§4.4](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-4)) and Chapter 5.

The thesis does not reduce mind, meaning, or value to physics: it establishes the structural minimum on which any account of mind, meaning, or value must stand.

Within the present modal constraint, Nature is the only coherent candidate for necessary existence: not because alternatives are ruled out by stipulation, but because any candidate examined at this level either resolves into structure under a different name or fails to ground any possible state of affairs. Any proposed necessary being is constrained by the same modal-status discipline.

The relevant necessary-being claim is therefore not settled by stipulation here. An objection of this shape, raised within the classical metaphysical tradition, is taken up again at [§5.2.1](rival-ultimates.html#sec-5-2-1) (*Divine Simplicity*), where its strongest formulations are tested against the same modal constraint.

*The broader Chapter 4 and Chapter 5 engagement with rival necessary-being candidates continues at [§5.1.1](rival-ultimates.html#sec-5-1-1) (Rasmussen's foundation argument), [§5.1.4](rival-ultimates.html#sec-5-1-4) (Swinburne), [§5.1.5](rival-ultimates.html#sec-5-1-5) (fine-tuning), [§5.3.1](rival-ultimates.html#sec-5-3-1) (Spinozist pantheism), [§5.3.2](rival-ultimates.html#sec-5-3-2) (Neoplatonism and the One), [§5.3.3](rival-ultimates.html#sec-5-3-3) (process theology), and [§5.1.9](rival-ultimates.html#sec-5-1-9) (Pizzi's impossibility of nothingness). Modal-structure objections to the necessity result itself are engaged at [§4.4.6](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-4-6) (Williamson's necessitism), [§4.4.7](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-4-7) (Sider's structuralism), and [§4.4.10](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-4-10) (Gasking's parody). Substrate-alternative candidates engaging the Necessity of Nature are taken up at [§4.3.5](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-5) (idealism), [§4.3.7](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-7) (Tegmark's mathematical universe), [§4.3.4](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-4) (cosmopsychism), and [§4.3.9](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-9) (structural realism). Existential-inertia naturalism (on which contingent existence persists by intrinsic inertia rather than by continuous conservation from an external necessary being) is the structurally adjacent position the framework's Φ-instantiation language brushes; Nature's persistence here runs through the structural role of Φ (the Substance Condition of [§1.4](groundwork.html#sec-1-4)), not through external conservation, and substantive engagement with the Schmid neo-classical / existential-inertia literature is taken up at [§4.2.9](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-2-9) (Existential Inertia).*

T, S, and Φ are not constraints on what physics permits within logical space. They are what logical space is made of. S5 does not describe a relationship between worlds standing apart from one another; it describes the outer limit of the one necessary structural ground within which all modal variation is internal.

The relation between modality and Nature is therefore not isomorphism but identity. Isomorphism would require two distinct domains with a structure-preserving correspondence between them; there is no second domain. The modal facts and the natural facts are not two structures sharing a form: they are one scope under two readings. This is the modal-monist commitment, inheriting the Triunity of Nature ([§2.6.9](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-9)): possibility, law, and being are not three layers but three logical-categorical readings of the structural Triconditions. The Triunity is established at [§2.6.9](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-9) for Reality as the change-hosting structural complex; Exclusivity of Nature is where it goes universal: that no candidate necessary ground stands outside the Triconditions, not even one specified as atemporal, is proven here, not assumed at [§2.6.9](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-9). The modal-monism named here is the same compression at the level of facts: modal facts are not facts about a separate domain that happens to align with Nature; they are facts about Nature read under the modal lens. The compression operates at the structural level (what makes possibility possible *is* what makes actuality actual), not at the propositional level (the *being possible* / *being actual* distinction survives at the propositional level: some propositions are possibly true without being actually true, and the Triunity does not collapse this distinction). Possibility ranges over Nature because there is nowhere else for it to range; necessity is Nature because there is no necessity outside □(T∧S∧Φ). To ground modality is therefore to ground Nature, and any candidate ground that proposes to lie behind modality proposes to lie outside Nature, which is ∅.

The conceivable and the possible have long been treated as separable spaces: a domain of conceivable beings whose modal status remains open, and a narrower domain of those that are actually possible. The Triconditional Identity closes the gap between them for the reason already supplied at [§3.1](convergence.html#sec-3-1) and [§2.6.6](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-6): a specification that lacks T, S, and Φ is not a wider conceivable item waiting for modal evaluation but the ∅-diagnostic under another description, and a possible world is not an alternative structure but a T/S/Φ-coherent configuration within the one structural ground. There is no domain of the conceivable that lies beyond Nature; the conceivable, when it is genuinely conceivable, is what Nature looks like read modally. The conceivable-versus-possible gap [@kripke1980; @chalmers2002; @yablo1993] is the standard contemporary location of the worry: some things seem conceivable that are not possible (water-without-H₂O on the Kripkean reading; a sphere of uranium-235 a mile in diameter on the Quinean reading). The Triconditional Identity does not collapse the gap by fiat. It locates where the gap operates: not between a wider domain of the conceivable and a narrower domain of the possible, but between a subset of *apparently* conceivable specifications that fail under scrutiny (those that turn out to specify ∅ or specify a structure that is not T/S/Φ-coherent) and the genuinely conceivable specifications (those that are genuinely possible because they specify T/S/Φ-coherent arrangements). The phrase 'when it is genuinely conceivable' is the restriction-marker for the genuine subset, not an unmotivated hedge. The classical ontological argument depended on the assumption that conceivability could outrun possibility: that one could conceive a being whose conception required its existence. The reading developed here locates where that assumption was load-bearing: it treated conceivability as a domain prior to and larger than Nature. The argument here gives reasons to think no such prior domain exists.

Any percept in view is there because something persists through the distance between observer and observed, something holds them apart, and something carries both forward through the moment. The structural Conditions are not a thesis about Reality applied to a world that could have been otherwise. They are the Conditions under which any such encounter takes place: Nature itself, in which *reading*, *sentence*, and *page* have anything to refer to. The proof identifies what any such encounter already requires.

::: {.theorem}
**Triconditional Identity** · **T5** · *Theorem 5*

Point at Nature and you are pointing at the necessary Conditions. Point at the necessary Conditions and you are pointing at necessary possibility. Point at necessary possibility and you are pointing at Nature. N ↔ □(T∧S∧Φ), N ↔ □◇C, □(T∧S∧Φ) ↔ □◇C. (restated from [§2.6.10](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-10))


:::

The Triconditional Cross-Entailment establishes that T, S, and Φ are one nomological fact constituted as three co-extensive Conditions. The Modal Identity establishes that this fact is analytically identical to the possibility of change. The Triconditional Identity names the whole: what the Triconditional Cross-Entailment establishes internally, and what the Modal Identity confirms externally, is Nature: necessarily, completely, and without remainder.

A further consequence follows directly from the Triconditional Identity. If structure is not a container within which things exist but the constitutive structure of existence itself (if T, S, and Φ *are* what Reality *consists in* rather than a structure things happen to occupy) then for any individual thing to exist is for it to be an instantiation of that structure. There is no position inside structure from which something could exist without being temporal, spatial, and physical, because structure has no inside that is not already *constituted* by those Conditions.

An entity that stood in no temporal, spatial, or physical relation to Nature would not, on the present modal constraint, transcend it; it would fall outside any possible world: the position the formal argument identifies with ∅. Whether a candidate that claims precisely such transcendence (a necessary being the theist places outside the natural order) can make that claim good against the modal structure is not settled here. That is the engagement of Chapter 6, and the verdict that Reality is Nature with no transcendent remainder is reserved until it is complete (Chapter 7).

::: {.column-margin .book-annotation-note}
**Natural worry.** Doesn't this settle the whole question—no God, case closed? Not here, and the book is careful to say so. The result holds within one modal constraint: any candidate examined at this structural level either resolves into structure under another name or fails to ground anything at all. But whether a necessary being might stand outside the natural order altogether—the transcendent God of classical theism—is explicitly not foreclosed at this stage; that's the burden of the later chapters. What's established now is narrower and still strong: within the space of grounds for possible states of affairs, structure is the only coherent occupant. The transcendence question is flagged, not answered.

:::


Exclusivity of Nature closes the same fork from a different direction: any proposed entity either instantiates T, S, and Φ (in which case it occupies Nature) or it does not (in which case it is not a coherent entity at all). There is no third option. Individual existence just is occupancy of the necessary structure.

::: {.corollary}
**Necessary Occupancy** · **R12** · *Result of T5 and T7*

For any individual thing to exist is for it to occupy the necessary structure: to be at a point in Time, somewhere in Space, and to persist as a causal relatum in Substance. This is not an external constraint imposed on existing things from outside. It is constitutive of what existence consists in. A putative entity that satisfies none of these Conditions is not a thing that exists in an unusual way. It is not a thing at all.


:::

*A note on “structural constitution” throughout this section.* The phrase “Reality’s necessary structural constitution” is used in the structural-functional sense throughout: T, S, and Φ are the co-constitutive requirements of any direction-involving, distinction-involving, and persistence-involving state of affairs, not an essence prior to or independent of the modal field from which modal truths follow. Whether that structural-functional identity can be kept stable against the pressure that it is a real definition under a different label is the question addressed at [§4.1.10](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-10).

Nature is not a metaphor for structure. It is Reality’s necessary structural constitution: the joint presence of T, S, and Φ that gives any direction, distinction, and persistence its content. The argument is not an image laid over Reality. It is what Reality is, derived from the Conditions any Reality must satisfy.

## 2.9 Precedent Convergence {#sec-2-9}

It is fair to ask whether a conclusion of this size stands alone. It does not: beginning with Spinoza and running through several modern programs, independent lines of philosophy have been arriving at much the same place from their own directions, in their own vocabularies. That agreement is evidence the conclusion is well grounded.

Chapter 2 has built the structural case from the inside. The result sits within a contemporary research program that has been independently converging on adjacent conclusions.

The historical anchor is Spinoza. The *Ethics* [-@spinoza1677] makes Nature (*Deus sive Natura*) the single necessary substance, derives modes from it by structural necessity, and grounds the modal field in nothing further. The present argument differs from Spinoza in vocabulary (T∧S∧Φ rather than substance/attribute/mode) and in method (modal logic over the structural Conditions rather than geometric deduction from definitions). It does not differ in the location of necessity (why contingency survives at the level of configurations despite the shared location of necessity is the question addressed at [§2.8.4](the-argument.html#sec-2-8-4) and [§2.8.5](the-argument.html#sec-2-8-5); the full Deus-sive-Natura engagement is at [§5.3.1](rival-ultimates.html#sec-5-3-1)). Four contemporary lines run parallel to the structural spine of the present argument and converge on adjacent conclusions from independent directions: priority monism ([§2.9.1](the-argument.html#sec-2-9-1)), the modal limits on necessary-being arguments ([§2.9.2](the-argument.html#sec-2-9-2)), the total-theory comparison against necessary-being arguments ([§2.9.3](the-argument.html#sec-2-9-3)), and contemporary necessitarianism ([§2.9.4](the-argument.html#sec-2-9-4)). A fifth convergence (older but structurally adjacent) is the independent maturation of three formal logics each settling along one of the Conditions ([§2.9.5](the-argument.html#sec-2-9-5)).

The convergence matters on four points. *First*, the present argument is not an isolated thesis but the joint of several independent inquiries. *Second*, the contemporary literature has been moving toward Nature as the locus of necessity without quite naming it; the structural-triconditional decomposition T∧S∧Φ supplied here is what those inquiries have been missing as the content of their conclusion. *Third*, the convergence works in two directions: each precedent strengthens the present argument by establishing that the move is independently motivated, and the present argument strengthens each precedent by supplying the structural content their conclusions require. *Fourth*, convergence with adjacent precedents in the necessity literature is not by itself the comparative-total-theories case against naturalism's rivals. Independent motivation establishes that the move is non-isolated; it does not establish that the move's total cost (ontological commitments, explanatory loss, tensions against background commitments) is lower than the alternatives. That comparative pricing is engaged at Chapter 4 under Oppy's comparative-total-theories discipline: the necessary-being family in Chapters 5 and 6, the modal-variant family at [§4.4](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-4), the physics/mind family at [§4.3](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3). The present catalog establishes literature convergence; Chapter 4 establishes comparative-cost superiority.

What the present argument adds to this program is not the conclusion but the architecture. The modal-invariance bottleneck ([§2.1](the-argument.html#sec-2-1)) supplies the modal closure. The bilateral-cogito chain (§[§2.2](the-argument.html#sec-2-2)–2.4) supplies the structural derivation of Temporality, Spatiality, and Physicality. The unity of T∧S∧Φ as the Triconditionality of Nature is supplied at [§2.6](the-argument.html#sec-2-6), identified under three Triconditional readings: Modal, Nomological, Ontological. The necessity declaration ([§2.8.5](the-argument.html#sec-2-8-5)) ties the formal theorem to the named Nature. The convergence is the contemporary literature recognizing in its own vocabulary what the longer project sets out in full.

Chapter 2 closes at [§2.10](the-argument.html#sec-2-10) by developing what the convergence makes available downstream: the three logics native to the three Conditions, the stratified scientific architecture they ground, and the metalogical position the framework owns. Chapter 3 then stress-tests the result through construction, performance, null-state closure, and grounding. It distinguishes genuinely independent lines from shared hinges, rebuilds role-level necessity without S5, and leaves proposition-wise □◇C with T1 unless a separate type-bridge is supplied. The convergence is therefore evidence of robustness where the lines separate, not a blanket claim of premise-disjoint overdetermination.[^2-9-0-precedent-convergence-ch4]

[^2-9-0-precedent-convergence-ch4]: The precedent literature is engaged dialectically in Chapter 4. Williamson's necessitism is the contemporary necessitist complement to the Della Rocca / Karofsky necessitarian line ([§4.4.6](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-4-6)), Rasmussen's foundation argument is the contemporary necessary-being program ([§5.1](rival-ultimates.html#sec-5-1)), and Spinozist pantheism carries the Deus-sive-Natura identification ([§5.3.1](rival-ultimates.html#sec-5-3-1)). Pizzi's impossibility of nothingness is the closest methodological cousin ([§4.1.11](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-11)), and modal fictionalism is where the modal-deflationist alternative is engaged ([§4.4.4](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-4-4)).

### 2.9.1 Priority Monism {#sec-2-9-1}

Schaffer's priority monism holds that the cosmos is the one fundamental object and is prior to its proper parts. @harrop2024 develops a modalized version of priority monism (priority monism enriched with the claim that the priority relation between the cosmos and its proper parts holds with metaphysical necessity). Harrop argues that this enrichment entails the necessary existence of the actual cosmos and the impossibility of any concrete object not actually instantiated. The argument turns on the grounding-theoretic premise that the prior is fundamental in any world it grounds, combined with the modalization that the grounding relation holds necessarily. Where Harrop reaches a necessary cosmos from grounding-theoretic premises and modal closure, the present argument reaches a necessary Nature from the fixed-domain derivation and its Bottleneck defense (§[§2.1.4](the-argument.html#sec-2-1-4)–2.1.5) and the bilateral-cogito chain (§[§2.2](the-argument.html#sec-2-2)–2.4). The two approaches converge on adjacent conclusions, but the theses are not identical. Harrop's thesis is that the *actual concrete cosmos* exists necessarily: a claim about the totality of concrete being. The present argument's thesis is that the *structural Conditions* T∧S∧Φ are necessary: a claim about the modal structure any cosmos must instantiate. The structural-conditions thesis is implied by the necessary-actual-cosmos thesis under the additional assumption that the actual cosmos instantiates T∧S∧Φ; the converse does not hold. A reader who finds Harrop's concrete-totality move too strong can accept the present argument's narrower structural-conditions claim without that commitment, and a reader who accepts Harrop's claim accepts the present argument's *a fortiori*. The structural specification the present argument adds is what Harrop's *necessary actual cosmos* would have to instantiate on either reading.

### 2.9.2 Modal Limits {#sec-2-9-2}

Van Hamme distinguishes three classes of necessity: logical-analytic (Class A), modal-structural (Class B), and existential (Class C), and argues that modal logic's jurisdiction stops at Class B. Arguments that ask modal apparatus to certify Class C necessity (that a particular being exists necessarily) cannot get that result without admitting Class B structure, which already does the work the proposed existent was supposed to do. Van Hamme reads the result as a limit on a family of necessary-being arguments; the present argument reads it as a relocation of modal force. What modal logic *can* deliver, Class B (modal-structural necessity, the necessity of frame-conditions any possible world satisfies), is the class T∧S∧Φ occupies. The identification is inclusive rather than exhaustive: Class B may include further frame-conditions the present argument does not develop, but T, S, and Φ are Class B necessities on the structural-minimum reading the present argument develops, since they are the frame-conditions any modally specifiable state of affairs satisfies. @fritzLoSchmid2026 run a structurally distinct reverse-direction modal ontological argument against a necessary-being conclusion, valid in S4 alone, without reliance on the Euclidean Axiom. The relevant comparison is with the fixed-domain modal-stability argument and its Bottleneck defense at §[§2.1.4](the-argument.html#sec-2-1-4)–2.1.5, not with [§2.1.3](the-argument.html#sec-2-1-3)'s non-vacuity lemma. Any claim that an S4-only reverse argument transfers to the present framework must be assessed against those premises rather than attributed to Modal Constitution. Three independent lines converge on the negative result: modal logic does not by itself deliver a particular necessary being. The present argument adds the positive complement: what modal logic does deliver is Nature.

### 2.9.3 Total-Theory Comparison {#sec-2-9-3}

Oppy's work develops the comparative-total-theories framework (assess metaphysical positions by their total cost in ontological commitments, explanatory loss, and tension against background commitments) and applies it to necessary-being arguments (Rasmussen, Pruss, Plantinga-style ontological) as competitors to naturalism. The verdict, on Oppy's accounting, is that the necessary-being family pays a higher total cost than the naturalist alternative because the necessary-being adds a being beyond Nature, whereas the naturalist makes Nature itself the terminus. The present argument relocates the necessity to Nature itself: T∧S∧Φ are necessary, and the question whether anything *further* is necessary (a particular being, a divine reality, a non-natural foundation) is taken up at length in Chapters 5 and 6 (the Theistic Counter-Constructions cluster). Oppy's comparative framework is the natural discipline for that question. The present argument's contribution is not a rival total theory but the structural specification naturalism's necessary terminus requires: the Conditions read along three Triconditional axes. Where Oppy's *naturalism* is articulated against the necessary-being alternatives, the present argument supplies what naturalism's necessary terminus consists in.

A further observation, which Oppy's own method surfaces: the comparison-of-total-theories framework itself requires stability — stable logical relations, inferential standards, and criteria by which one theory can be priced against another. Initial-state naturalism posits Nature as modally contingent, its structural character unrequired; but a modally contingent inferential framework is one that might have been otherwise, in which case the comparison would yield a different result. The comparison market is not neutral ground. Coherently pricing initial-state naturalism against the Necessity of Nature already runs on the kind of structural necessity the present argument posits: T∧S∧Φ are the conditions under which logical and inferential relations have a domain to operate on. This is not the claim that logical necessity and structural necessity are identical; they are distinct. It is the claim that the stability of the comparison framework depends on the structural conditions being instantiated, and that those conditions are what T∧S∧Φ name. Initial-state naturalism can be entertained as a theoretical rival; it cannot be coherently priced without presupposing what the necessity claim provides.

### 2.9.4 Contemporary Necessitarianism {#sec-2-9-4}

Two related but distinct lines defend strong necessitarian theses. Della Rocca [-@dellaRocca2010; -@dellaRocca2020] revives the Principle of Sufficient Reason and argues that PSR commits its proponent to the necessity of all states of affairs; the conclusion is presented as a consequence of taking PSR seriously rather than as an independently motivated necessitarian thesis. Karofsky's *A Case for Necessitarianism* [-@karofsky2021] defends the stronger thesis directly: *everything* is necessary, with no contingency anywhere in the modal field. The two lines converge on overlapping conclusions but proceed differently: Della Rocca through PSR-revival, Karofsky through direct necessitarian argument. The present argument does not endorse this stronger thesis ([§2.8.4](the-argument.html#sec-2-8-4), *Necessity Precedes Contingency*); the modal floor is necessary, the modal contents are not. But the necessitarian's case strengthens the present argument's narrower claim from both directions. If the necessitarian is right that everything is necessary, then *a fortiori* the structural Conditions of Nature are necessary, and the present argument's conclusion is contained in the necessitarian's stronger one. If the necessitarian is wrong about modal contents, the case for the structural Conditions' necessity remains untouched, because the present argument never required global necessity to begin with. Della Rocca and Karofsky press from one direction; the present argument fills in the structural specification their general thesis leaves open.

### 2.9.5 Three Formal Logics {#sec-2-9-5}

Two recognized formal families and one synthetic umbrella align with the three existence-axes the present argument identifies as the Conditions. Temporal logic regiments inferences over T, and spatial logic regiments inferences over S. The Φ-axis is distributed across formal ontology, mereology, classical first-order logic with identity, and substance metaphysics. The present argument gathers those traditions under the coined label *substantial logic*: the *logic of being qua being* in Aristotle's sense (*Metaphysics* Γ 1003a21), read specifically through persistence, identity, and part–whole structure. The convergence is therefore not that three literatures independently adopted the same three labels. It is that independently developed formal work clusters along T and S as established disciplines and along Φ across several traditions that the framework synthesizes. *Three Formally Distinct Logics* ([§2.10.1](the-argument.html#sec-2-10-1)) develops that derivation and states the coined status of the Φ-axis explicitly.

## 2.10 Three Logical Strata {#sec-2-10}

Independent inquiries have been converging on the present account from their own directions ([§2.9](the-argument.html#sec-2-9)). That convergence is no coincidence, and the reason it is not lies in [§2.6.11](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-11).

Condition-Individuation supplies a two-clause screen for Condition-status (determinacy plus LEM along an existence-axis, and irreducibility). It shows that T, S, and Φ pass the screen and places a precise burden on any proposed fourth; as clarified in [§2.6.11](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-11), entailment by the three does not alone prove reducibility, so the screen does not deductively establish that no further irreducible axis is possible. Nor does the screen by itself generate three consequence relations. What it motivates is three axis-specific formal disciplines: temporal logic native to T, spatial logic native to S, and the substantial-logic umbrella native to Φ. Their formal differentiation comes from the operators, axioms, and semantics required by each axis's upstream structure, together with the independently developed literatures of Prior, Tarski, Leśniewski, Quine, Simons, Lowe, and others. The clustering is downstream confirmation, not a proof extracted from LEM alone.

The Triconditionality of Nature carries three logics native to its three Conditions. Physics is empirical-nomological work conducted within the joint apparatus of those three, the *modal structure*: the fixed structure of what is and is not possible that □(T∧S∧Φ) defines. Metaphysics is the root-layer discipline that articulates the logics' grounding in Reality's structure. The convergence happens because the three Conditions are real, the disciplines tracking them are the formal logics native to each, and those three logics jointly constitute one modal structure.

The modal structure established here is structural (what any possible Reality must instantiate to be a Reality) not a phenomenal explanation. Whether consciousness fits this structure is the question of [§4.3.1](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-1) and Chapter 8, not of Chapter 2.

Chapter 3 then tests the framework on the terms set at the close of [§2.9](the-argument.html#sec-2-9), recording where its independent lines genuinely separate and where they share the role-level identifications established here.[^2-10-0-three-logical-strata-ch4]

[^2-10-0-three-logical-strata-ch4]: [§4.1.8](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-8) engages ontological deflationism and [§4.1.9](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-9) takes up Wittgensteinian quietism, the Chapter 4 meta-philosophical objections to the framework's commitments; [§4.3.9](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-9) handles structural realism, the structural-realist alternative engaging the metaphysical-structuralist commitments.

### 2.10.1 Three Distinct Logics {#sec-2-10-1}

Condition-Individuation supports three axis-specific formal disciplines in two stages. First, its determinacy-plus-LEM clause and irreducibility clause distinguish T, S, and Φ as three admitted domains of inquiry. Second, the native structure of each axis motivates a specialized formal apparatus. The result is temporal, spatial, and substantial logic — three disciplines with different target vocabularies and formal resources, sharing whatever classical floor the framework separately defends.

Stage one individuates axes, not consequence relations. Irreducibility means that the content of T-claims does not reduce without remainder to S- or Φ-content. It does not follow that one background logic cannot govern claims from all three domains, or that non-reducible predicates require non-intertranslatable logics. The legitimate conclusion at this stage is weaker: each axis calls for its own theory-specific vocabulary and axiomatization if its native structure is to be represented.

Stage two supplies that differentiation. T carries temporal modalities (succession, precedence, simultaneity); S carries spatial relations (region, inclusion, connection, proximity); Φ carries identity, persistence, and part/whole. The native structure is supplied by the upstream derivations at §[§1.4](groundwork.html#sec-1-4) and 2.4–2.6, not by LEM. Formal systems regimenting those structures can therefore differ in syntax, axioms, and semantics. Temporal logic and spatial logic are established disciplines; *substantial logic* is the framework's synthetic umbrella over several traditions. The claim earned is discipline-level formal differentiation, not a deduction that Reality contains exactly three mutually exclusive logics merely because it contains three irreducible axes.

The distinctness shows in a single ordinary claim. Take *the cup was on the table before you drank from it*. Three inferences run through it at once, along three axes. *Before you drank* is temporal: it places the resting earlier than the drinking, licensing inferences of precedence and tense (T). *On the table* is spatial: it locates the cup in contact with and supported by the surface, licensing inferences of region, contact, and inclusion (S). *The cup* — the same one throughout — is substantial: one persisting bearer across both the resting and the drinking, not two cups sharing a name, licensing inferences of identity and persistence (Φ). None of the three cashes out in another's vocabulary: *before* is not a region, *on* is not a moment, and *the same cup* is neither a time nor a place. Restate the precedence in the spatial apparatus and you have changed the subject, not translated it — the axis-level irreducibility Condition-Individuation establishes, met in a single sentence. Three logics, no common coin.

The literature delivers exactly this. Temporal logic is a mature formal discipline [@prior1957; @prior1967; @pnueli1977; @goldblatt1992] with operators F, P, G, H tracking future, past, always, and sometime; branching-time versus linear-time families axiomatize different commitments about T-structure. Spatial logic is similarly mature [@tarski1959 on topology in formal language; @randellCuiCohn1992 on region-connection calculus; @aielloPrattHartmannVanBenthem2007 *Handbook of Spatial Logics*] with operators for region, inclusion, connection, proximity. Substantial logic, the present argument's umbrella term for the formal-ontology, mereology, classical-identity, and substance-metaphysics literatures that together cover the Φ-axis (the *logic of being qua being* in Aristotle's sense, *Metaphysics* Γ 1003a21), is the author's coinage rather than a label any of those literatures use of themselves. The term is licensed by the role the literatures jointly play (regimenting bivalent inference over the existence-axis of persistence-and-identity) rather than by any prior unification under the label. Under that umbrella the literatures are developed under several rubrics: formal ontology [@husserl1900 *Logical Investigations*; @smith2003], mereology [@lesniewski1916; @simons1987 *Parts*], classical first-order logic with identity [@quine1960 *Word and Object*], and substance metaphysics [@wiggins2001 *Sameness and Substance Renewed*; @lowe2006 *The Four-Category Ontology*]. Each was developed by working logicians and ontologists without the framework's metaphysics in hand.

That working logicians and ontologists who were not consulting the present framework converged on three formal disciplines settling exactly along the three existence-axes Condition-Individuation individuates is itself a striking fact. The clustering is read at [§2.9](the-argument.html#sec-2-9) as another case of the precedent-convergence pattern; the forward derivation explains why they settled where they did. The three logics are taken as the root layer of the stratified scientific architecture at [§2.10.2](the-argument.html#sec-2-10-2). The metalogical position the foregoing derivation owns (logic as metaphysically grounded, structurally individuated, realist, and foundational to the sciences) is made explicit at [§2.10.3](the-argument.html#sec-2-10-3).[^2-10-1-three-logics-ch4]

[^2-10-1-three-logics-ch4]: The three-logics derivation (temporal, spatial, and substantial logic as axis-individuated formal disciplines) is engaged in Chapter 4. Quine is the principal substantial-logic ancestor and the divergence point on whether identity is one discipline among many or part of classical first-order logic *simpliciter* ([§4.1.6](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-6)). Conventionalism asks whether axis-individuation is structural rather than chosen ([§4.1.7](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-7)); structural realism (Ladyman & Ross) is the closest ally on Reality's carvable joints, diverging on whether the joints are these three ([§4.3.9](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-9)); mereological nihilism asks whether substantial logic has anything composite to regiment ([§4.3.11](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-11)); and Tegmark asks whether the three logics are mathematical structures rather than features of Reality ([§4.3.7](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-7)).

### 2.10.2 The Stratified Architecture {#sec-2-10-2}

The three logics established in [§2.10.1](the-argument.html#sec-2-10-1) are not one tier among other disciplines. Together they form the root of a stratified scientific architecture. Temporal, spatial, and substantial logic regiment claims along three irreducible existence-axes; every further inquiry therefore operates within their joint constraints.

The stratification adds no new premise to the proof. It draws out the architecture implicit in the three-logic result. A discipline occupies a higher stratum by adding distinctive content, vocabulary, and methods to the constraints supplied below. Lower strata constrain what can coherently be said at higher ones, but they do not derive the higher strata's characteristic claims.

*The strata.*

- *Root layer.* LEM applied at existence-axes. The bare logical floor; bivalent existence-claims are determinate at each of the three axes.
- *Layer 1.* The three logics. Temporal, spatial, substantial: each carving its axis's native structure within LEM-bivalence. Condition-Individuation's irreducibility clause keeps them distinct.
- *Layer 2.* Physics. Empirical-nomological work within the joint engagement of all three logics. Conservation laws, dynamics, field equations, particles, constants: physics-specific content that operates within the three-logic scaffold but is not derivable from it.
- *Layer 3.* Higher empirical sciences. Chemistry (patterns of atomic Φ-beings governed by physics), biology (organized Φ-systems exhibiting metabolism, reproduction), astronomy (large-scale T-S-Φ patterns), each engaging some subset of physics's content as input.
- *Layer 4.* Human and social sciences. Psychology, sociology, economics, history: patterns within the lower layers' content.

At each layer the deeper layers act as constraints, not as content. Physics does not derive from the three logics; it operates within them. Chemistry does not derive from physics; it operates within physics's nomological content. The architecture is stratified rather than reductive: no stratum reduces to the one beneath; each contributes distinctive claims, vocabulary, and methods constrained by but not supplied by the deeper strata.

*Physics is empirical-nomological work within the three logics, not identical to them.* This is worth stating sharply because the temptation to identify physics with the three logics is real and the identification is mistaken. Physics presupposes and uses the three logics: any physical claim is about a Φ-being at an S-position over T-succession, regimented by the inferential apparatus the three logics supply. But physics adds empirical content (specific laws, constants, particles, fields), nomological structure (causation, dynamics, conservation principles), specific mathematical apparatus (calculus, differential geometry, tensor analysis, group theory), and methodology (experiment, prediction, theory-revision). The three logics supply none of this. They supply the framework within which all of this is conducted.

The cleaner formulation: physics is *empirical-nomological investigation conducted within the joint apparatus of temporal, spatial, and substantial logic*. Not identity (physics = three logics combined), but containment (physics = three logics + empirical-nomological work). This formulation also tightens the anti-physicalism of [§2.8.3](the-argument.html#sec-2-8-3): physicalism conflates Layer 2's content (specific laws, particles) with the root layer and Layer 1 (the three logics that physics is conducted within). The mistake is treating Layer 2's content as foundational when its foundations lie a stratum below.

*The location of metaphysics.* The stratification places metaphysics correctly. Metaphysics is not a high-level science built on top of physics; it is not in competition with physics over the same explanatory territory; it is not empty speculation about what physics already settles. Metaphysics is the discipline whose object is the root layer and Layer 1: the three Conditions and Condition-Individuation's individuation of them. Its method is conceptual analysis of LEM-application, irreducibility-testing across candidate axes, and the structural derivations Chapter 2 conducts. That method has its own validity-conditions and its own object, distinct from physics's.

Critics who treat metaphysics as disguised physics or empty speculation include logical positivists [@carnap1928 *The Logical Structure of the World*; @carnap1932 *The Elimination of Metaphysics Through Logical Analysis of Language*], Quine in some moods [-@quine1948], and naturalized metaphysicians who locate metaphysics within or below empirical science [@ladymanRoss2007 *Every Thing Must Go*]. Each criticism preserves part of the right discipline while locating it at the wrong level.

Positivism is right that metaphysical claims require clear criteria; Chapter 2 supplies them through explicit conceptual and structural derivations. Quine is right that ontology should track the values of bound variables in our best theories; the further claim is that those values must instantiate the three Conditions. Ladyman and Ross are right that metaphysics should answer to the structure scientific inquiry presupposes; the disagreement concerns where that structure lies.

On the present architecture, physics already presupposes the three-logical root. It cannot investigate that root without employing the very logic under examination. Metaphysics therefore has a distinct object and method. It is neither disguised physics nor speculation unconstrained by physics.

The stratification also explains why the unity-of-science program had the right intuition but the wrong root. The intuition [@carnap1934 *The Unity of Science*; @neurath1944 *Foundations of the Social Sciences*; @hempel1969 *Reduction: Ontological and Linguistic Facets*; @oppenheimPutnam1958 *Unity of Science as a Working Hypothesis*] was that there is a single underlying structure that the sciences all rely on. The mistake was putting physics at the bottom.[^2-10-2-stratified-architecture-ch4] The framework's correction: the root is the three logics, and physics is Layer 2, not Layer 0. Levels-of-reality work [@putnam1967 *Psychological Predicates*; @fodor1974 *Special Sciences*; @wimsatt1976 *Reductionism, Levels of Organization, and the Mind-Body Problem*; @kim1998 *Mind in a Physical World*] comes closer; it recognizes stratification without strict reduction, but still typically treats physics as the foundational level rather than as Layer 2 above the three logics. The framework's stratification keeps the levels-of-reality insight while relocating the foundation.

[^2-10-2-stratified-architecture-ch4]: The stratified architecture (physics as Layer 2 rather than Layer 0, metaphysics as the discipline of the root layer and Layer 1, and the anti-physicalist relocation of the foundation) is engaged in Chapter 4. Structural realism (Ladyman & Ross's *Every Thing Must Go*) is the naturalized-metaphysics position the framework partially agrees with and parts from on where the joints lie ([§4.3.9](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-9)); Quine, on ontology tracking bound-variable values, meets the framework's reply that the values must instantiate the three Conditions ([§4.1.6](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-6)); Tegmark asks whether the root is mathematical rather than logical ([§4.3.7](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-7)); eliminativism presses on metaphysics as a legitimate discipline ([§4.3.2](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-2)); and governing-law accounts (Armstrong, Dretske, and Tooley's necessitation-relation accounts) are the non-Humean alternative on whether laws govern Layer 2 ([§4.1.4](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-4)).

### 2.10.3 The Metalogical Position {#sec-2-10-3}

The foregoing argument owns a substantive metalogical position: a position *about* logic, not a contribution *within* logic. The framework proposes no new axioms, no new operators, no new semantic clauses; temporal logic, spatial logic, and the formal-ontology and mereology traditions already exist as developed by Prior, Tarski, Leśniewski, Quine, Simons, Lowe, and others. What the framework offers is a theory of why there is logic at all, and why these particular logics. The position has four commitments.

*Logic is metaphysically grounded.* The framework ties its classical inferential floor to a joint determinacy-and-LEM commitment along T, S, and Φ. LEM is the Law of Excluded Middle; it does not by itself entail that every claim takes exactly one of two semantic values, so bivalence is an additional commitment rather than a gloss on LEM. The framework rejects the alternative metalogical foundations on offer. Logic is not convention (against Carnap-style pluralism, *The Logical Syntax of Language* [-@carnap1937]; the three logics are dictated by Reality's axes, not chosen for utility). Logic is not transcendental condition of thought (against Kant [-@kant1781] *Critique of Pure Reason*; the framework grounds logic in Reality, not in mind). Logic is not free-floating formalism (against Hilbert [-@hilbert1899] *Foundations of Geometry* on formalist readings; logic has real referents, per the reverse derivation at [§2.9](the-argument.html#sec-2-9)). Logic is not psychological construction for empirical existence-claims (against intuitionist treatments of empirical bivalence; @brouwer1907 and @heyting1956 raise legitimate concerns about unbounded mathematical claims, but the framework restricts its LEM-application to existence-claims along the three Conditions, where the bivalence is empirical not unbounded-mathematical).

Each rejected position captures something real that the framework preserves. Carnap is right that higher-stratum axiomatic choice has a conventional moment; the framework's anti-conventionalism applies only to the floor LEM and the three axis-logics, not to choices among axiom systems above them. Kant is right that logical structure shows up wherever cognition occurs; the framework adds that the cognizer is a T-S-Φ instantiator, so cognition tracks logic because both track Reality. Hilbert is right that the formal disciplines admit consistent axiomatization independently of semantic interpretation; the framework adds that, for the three logics, the axiomatizations also have real referents per the reverse derivation at [§2.9](the-argument.html#sec-2-9).

*Logic is structurally individuated.* There are exactly as many basic logics as Reality has existence-axes. Three: temporal, spatial, and substantial. The modal axis is screened out by Condition-Individuation's irreducibility clause ([§2.6.11](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-11)): the Modal Identity identifies □◇C with □(T∧S∧Φ), so the modal-axis is the modal-side of the same Nature rather than a fourth independent axis. Not arbitrarily many: the framework rejects unrestricted logical pluralism [@beallRestall2006 *Logical Pluralism*], according to which any number of logics are correct for any number of domains with no metaphysical privileging. The three logics are axis-individuated, not domain-individuated: what counts as an axis is determined by the Lemma's two-clause screen, not by pragmatic choice. Not just one: the framework also rejects unrestricted logical monism, according to which a single logic is the one true logic. LEM at the bare floor is shared across axes, but each axis develops its own axioms beyond LEM, and those axiom-systems are not inter-translatable.

*Logic has real referents.* The claims of temporal, spatial, and substantial logic are determinately true or false because they are about real features of Reality. The framework is realist about the three formal disciplines. This realism extends the realism about Nature established at [§2.8](the-argument.html#sec-2-8): just as Nature is real — not a useful construct, theoretical posit, or regulative ideal — the three Conditions are real, and so are the inferential systems native to them. This is the realism the reverse derivation in [§2.9](the-argument.html#sec-2-9) needs to do its work (a formal discipline has determinately true-or-false claims only if its claims have real referents), and the framework owns it as a substantive commitment rather than a methodological convenience. That the commitment is more than a posit (that logic's referents are real rather than framework-relative) is defended against the strongest deflationary challenge at [§4.1.8](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-8), on the deflationist's own criterion of objectivity.

*Logic is foundational to the sciences.* Logic is the root layer of the stratified architecture developed at [§2.10.2](the-argument.html#sec-2-10-2). Physics is Layer 2: empirical-nomological work conducted within the three logics; higher sciences branch from physics. This commitment is anti-physicalist in a specific way: physics does not ground logic; logic grounds physics. And it is anti-scientistic in a specific way: metaphysics is not eliminable in favor of empirical science; metaphysics is the discipline of the root layer, with its own object and method that empirical science presupposes but cannot itself articulate.

*The shared classical floor.* The four commitments together describe a nested structure within the stratified architecture rather than competing horizontal options. The framework adopts both LEM and determinacy/bivalence for the targeted existence-claims along T, S, and Φ. The classical inferential apparatus follows from that package and the consequence rules separately adopted, not from LEM alone. Above the shared LEM floor, each axis develops its own axiom-system encoding its native structure: temporal modalities for T, region-relations for S, identity-and-persistence for Φ. The three axiom-systems are not inter-translatable above the LEM floor (per the Lemma's irreducibility clause), but they share the bivalent inferential floor below. The framework is therefore neither one-true-logic monism (one axiom-system across all domains) nor unrestricted pluralism (any number of logics for any number of domains by pragmatic choice); it is LEM-monist at the floor and axiom-system-pluralist above, with the pluralism dictated by Reality's existence-axes rather than by convention. This shared LEM floor is what allows the framework to keep the bivalent inferential apparatus universally binding on existence-claims while admitting axis-specific structure native to each Condition.

*The answer to the foundational question of philosophy of logic.* Where does logical normativity come from? Philosophy of logic has long asked. Frege [-@frege1879 *Begriffsschrift*; -@frege1893 *Grundgesetze der Arithmetik*] located it in the Third Realm of abstract objects. Wittgenstein's early *Tractatus* [-@wittgenstein1921] located it in the limits of representable language. Wittgenstein's late *Philosophical Investigations* [-@wittgenstein1953] located it in linguistic practice. Quine [-@quine1951 *Two Dogmas of Empiricism*; -@quine1969 *Epistemology Naturalized*] located it in the web of belief. Kant [-@kant1781] located it in transcendental conditions of cognition. Logical anti-exceptionalism [@williamson2017 *Doing Philosophy*; @hjortland2017 *Anti-exceptionalism About Logic*] locates it in continuity with empirical science.

The framework's answer: logical normativity comes from Reality's three existence-axes. Its classical floor is binding on the targeted existence-claims because clause 1 of the [§2.6.11](the-argument.html#sec-2-6-11) criterion combines determinacy with LEM; neither component should be treated as deriving the other. The three logics are binding on claims within their domains because each axis carries its native structure (the axioms regimenting its native modalities). The normativity is grounded in what Reality is: not in convention, not in mind, not in language, not in practice, not in web-of-belief. The framework is therefore a *metaphysical-grounding* account of logical normativity.

*Engagement-table.* How the framework's metalogical position stands relative to the existing options in philosophy of logic. *Rejected* marks a position the framework denies; *partial* marks a position the framework affirms on one point and parts from on another.

- *Conventionalism / Carnapian pluralism* [@carnap1937]: rejected. The three logics are not conventional choices; they are dictated by Reality's axes.
- *Formalism* (Hilbert, on formalist readings): rejected. Logic has real referents per the reverse derivation of [§2.9](the-argument.html#sec-2-9).
- *Logicism* [@frege1879; @russellWhitehead1910]: partial. Logic is foundational, but to all empirical inquiry, not just to mathematics.
- *Intuitionism* [@brouwer1907; @heyting1956]: partial. LEM may fail for unbounded mathematical claims; it applies determinately to existence-claims along the three Conditions.
- *Unrestricted logical pluralism* [@beallRestall2006]: rejected. Exactly three basic logics, axis-individuated, not arbitrarily many.
- *Logical monism* (single true logic): partial. LEM at the bare floor is shared; axis-specific axiom-systems differentiate.
- *Logical anti-exceptionalism* [@williamson2017; @hjortland2017]: partial. Logic is continuous with metaphysics (root-layer inquiry), not directly with empirical science; the sciences operate within logic but do not revise logic from above.
- *Structural realism / naturalized metaphysics* [@sider2011 *Writing the Book of the World*; @ladymanRoss2007 *Every Thing Must Go*]: partial. The framework agrees Reality has joints to be carved; it disagrees about which joints and about the relationship of metaphysics to physics. The framework's joints are the three Conditions, and metaphysics is the root-layer discipline distinct from any empirical science.

The framework's metalogical position combines four commitments: metaphysical grounding (the logics' normativity from Reality), structural individuation (exactly three basic logics, by Reality's existence-axes), realism (about the disciplines' referents), and foundationalism (logic as the root layer of the sciences).[^2-10-3-metalogical-position-ch4]

*The position's existential reach.* The four commitments do work beyond the metalogical question: they yield a convergence line confirming the necessity already declared at [§2.8.5](the-argument.html#sec-2-8-5). The line is *confirming-and-consistent* rather than *independent*: it runs through earlier framework machinery (the cogito chain at [§2.8.2](the-argument.html#sec-2-8-2) and the further [§3.3](convergence.html#sec-3-3) development of we-are-T-S-Φ-instantiators) rather than around it, and reaches the same modal conclusion through a different inferential path. If the three logics are necessary (commitment 1: grounded in Reality's existence-axes, not contingent on convention or mind) and have real referents (commitment 3: the disciplines' claims are about real features of Reality), then what the three logics describe is necessary. T-logic is the logic *of* T, not a logic *over* contents drawn from some independent T-domain; the necessity of T-logic and the necessity of T as a real feature of Reality are not two facts but one. Logic and Reality stand as map and terrain: distinguishable as modes of articulation, not as separate structures; the necessity that runs through the map is the necessity that runs through the terrain. The same holds for S-logic and Φ-logic. We are T-S-Φ instantiators: we exist along all three axes; we act, persist, and change as the entities the three logics describe ([§2.8.2](the-argument.html#sec-2-8-2) *Cogito Ergo Muto*; the point is developed further at [§3.3](convergence.html#sec-3-3)). The closure follows: we instantiate what is necessarily described. Our structural Conditions are necessary even where our particular instantiation is contingent ([§2.8.4](the-argument.html#sec-2-8-4) *Necessity Precedes Contingency*). The chapter's metalogical position is therefore a convergence line confirming the necessity declaration already made at [§2.8.5](the-argument.html#sec-2-8-5): not by way of the change-bottleneck and the structural-Conditions argument, but by way of logic's necessity transferring through realism-about-logic to the axes the logics are *of*. The convergence instantiates the precedent-convergence pattern catalogued at [§2.9](the-argument.html#sec-2-9) across the chapter's outward-facing literature, this time arising within the framework's own architecture rather than between the framework and contemporary work. The two lines converge on the same modal conclusion from different directions: Reality carries three Conditions, the Conditions are necessary, and we participate in their necessity at the structural level.

[^2-10-3-metalogical-position-ch4]: The metalogical position (logic as metaphysically grounded, structurally individuated, realist, and foundational to the sciences) is engaged across several Chapter 4 sections. Carnap-style conventionalism is the principal rejected alternative on the source of logical normativity ([§4.1.7](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-7)); Quine presses web-of-belief and naturalized epistemology ([§4.1.6](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-6)); Sider's *Writing the Book of the World* is the closest structural-realist neighbor, with divergent joint-carving ([§4.4.7](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-4-7)); Ladyman and Ross's naturalized metaphysics is the partial-agreement reference for the metaphysics-physics relation ([§4.3.9](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-9)); Tegmark asks whether logic is mathematical rather than metaphysical ([§4.3.7](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-3-7)); quietism and logical anti-exceptionalism are pressed by @williamson2017 and @hjortland2017 ([§4.1.9](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-9)); and deflationist accounts target logic's normativity ([§4.1.8](metaphysical-rivals.html#sec-4-1-8)).
